records.arabic:
بن مالك بن كعب بن النحاط بالنون والمهملة بن كعب بن حارثة بن غنم بن السلم بن امرئ القيس بن مالك بن أوس الأنصاري الأوسي يكنى أبا خيثمة وكان أحد النقباء بالعقبة ذكره بن إسحاق وغيره وساق بإسناده عن كعب بن مالك قال لما كانت الليلة التي واعدنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيها بمنى للبيعة اجتمعنا بالعقبة فأتانا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم واتبعه العباس وحده فقال اخرجوا إلي منكم اثني عشر نقيبا فذكرهم وفيه وكان نقيب بني عمرو بن عوف سعد بن خيثمة وروى البخاري في التاريخ من طريق رباح بن أبي معروف سمعت المغيرة بن حكيم سألت عبد الله بن سعد بن خيثمة هل شهدت بدرا قال نعم والعقبة ولقد كنت رديف أبي وكان نقيبا وقال بن إسحاق في المغازي نزل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بقباء على كلثوم بن الهدم وكان إذا خرج منه جلس للناس في بيت سعد بن خيثمة وكان يقال له بيت الغراب وقال بن إسحاق استشهد سعد بن خيثمة يوم بدر وقال موسى بن عقبة عن بن شهاب استهم يوم بدر سعد بن خيثمة وابنه سعد فخرج سهم سعد فقال له أبوه يا بني آثرني اليوم فقال سعد يا أبت لو كان غير الجنة فعلت فخرج سعد إلي بدر فقتل بها وقتل أبوه خيثمة يوم أحد وروى بن المبارك بإسناد له إلى سليمان بن أبان نحو هذه القصة واختلف في قاتله طعيمة بن عدي وقيل عمرو بن عبد ود وزعم أبو نعيم بن سعد بن خيثمة هذا هو أبو خيثمة الذي تخالف يوم تبوك ثم لحق وساق في ترجمته من طريق إبراهيم بن عبد الله بن خيثمة عن أبيه عن جده قال تخلفت في غزوة تبوك وساق لقصة والحق أنه غيره لاطباق أهل السير على أن صاحب هذه الترجمة استشهد ببدر وأورد بن منده وأبو نعيم في هذه الترجمة حديثا آخر من طريق إبراهيم أيضا وهووهم وقال أبو جعفر بن حبيب في قول حسان بن ثابت
أروني سعودا كالسعود التي سمت
بمكة من أولاد عمرو بن عامر
أقاموا عماد الدين حتى تمكنت
قواعده بالمرهفات البواتر قال أراد بالسعود سبعة وهم أربعة من الأوس وثلاثة بن الخزرج من الخزرج سعد بن عبادة وسعد بن الربيع وسعد بن عثمان أبو عبادة ومن الأوس سعد بن معاذ وسعد بن خيثمة وسعد بن عبيد وسعد بن زيد
records.english:
ibn Mālik ibn Kaʿb ibn al-Naḥāṭ—with nūn and undotted ḥāʾ—ibn Kaʿb ibn Ḥārithah ibn Ghanm ibn al-Salm ibn Imriʾ al-Qays ibn Mālik ibn Aws, al-Anṣārī al-Awsī. His kunya was Abū Khaythamah, and he was one of the representatives at al-ʿAqabah. Ibn Isḥāq and others mentioned him.

Ibn Isḥāq related, with his chain from Kaʿb ibn Mālik, who said: “On the night when we had arranged to meet the Messenger of God ﷺ at Minā to pledge allegiance, we gathered at al-ʿAqabah. The Messenger of God ﷺ came to us, with only al-ʿAbbās following him, and said: ‘Bring forward to me twelve representatives from among you.’” He then listed them; the account includes: “The representative of Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf was Saʿd ibn Khaythamah.”

Al-Bukhārī narrated in al-Tārīkh through Ribāḥ ibn Abī Maʿrūf: I heard al-Mughīrah ibn Ḥakīm say: I asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Khaythamah, “Did you witness Badr?” He said: “Yes, and al-ʿAqabah. I was riding behind my father, and he was a representative.”

Ibn Isḥāq said in al-Maghāzī: The Messenger of God ﷺ lodged at Qubāʾ with Kulthūm ibn al-Hidm. When he left that lodging, he would sit to receive people in the house of Saʿd ibn Khaythamah, which was called the House of the Raven.

Ibn Isḥāq said: Saʿd ibn Khaythamah was martyred on the day of Badr. Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah reported from Ibn Shihāb: On the day of Badr, Saʿd ibn Khaythamah and his son Saʿd drew lots. Saʿd's lot came out. His father said to him, “My son, give me preference today.” Saʿd replied, “My father, if it were anything other than Paradise, I would.” Saʿd went out to Badr and was killed there, while his father Khaythamah was killed on the day of Uḥud.

Editorial note: The opening of this report names “Saʿd ibn Khaythamah and his son Saʿd,” but its ending calls the father Khaythamah. The 1905–1907 ACO edition, volume 2, entry 3142, pages 75–76, retains the same conflicting names. They are left as written here; the two participants' relationship in the opening remains uncertain.

Ibn al-Mubārak narrated a similar story with a chain of his reaching Sulaymān ibn Abān. There is disagreement over his killer: Ṭuʿaymah ibn ʿAdī, or, it is said, ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Wudd.

Abū Nuʿaym claimed that this Saʿd ibn Khaythamah was Abū Khaythamah, who stayed behind on the occasion of Tabūk and then caught up.

Editorial note: This sentence follows the readings أن سعد (“that Saʿd”) and تخلف (“stayed behind”) in the 1905–1907 ACO edition, volume 2, page 76, entry 3142. The Arabic base instead has بن سعد and تخالف; those letters have not been changed in the Arabic.

In his biography he related, through Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khaythamah, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: “I stayed behind on the expedition to Tabūk”; he then related the story. The truth is that he was a different man, since the biographers unanimously agree that the subject of this biography was martyred at Badr. Ibn Mandah and Abū Nuʿaym included another hadith in this biography, also through Ibrāhīm; this is an error.

Abū Jaʿfar ibn Ḥabīb said, concerning the words of Ḥassān ibn Thābit:

Show me Saʿds like the Saʿds who rose high
at Mecca, of the descendants of ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir.
They raised religion's pillar until firmly planted
were its foundations, by the keen and cleaving blades.

He said: By “the Saʿds” he meant seven men: four from al-Aws and three from al-Khazraj. Those from al-Khazraj were Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah, Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ, and Saʿd ibn ʿUthmān, Abū ʿUbādah. Those from al-Aws were Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, Saʿd ibn Khaythamah, Saʿd ibn ʿUbayd, and Saʿd ibn Zayd.

records.english: Abū Khaythamah, who stayed behind at Tabūk. He has been mentioned in the preceding biography and will appear in the section on kunyās. He is better known by his kunya. His name is also said to have been Mālik ibn Qays. He was of al-Khazraj, whereas the man in the preceding biography was of al-Aws.

records.arabic: الدوسي قال بن حبان له صحبة وروى أحمد وابن أبي شيبة من طريق بسر بن عبد الله عن أبيه عن سعد بن أبي ذباب قال أتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأسلمت فاستعملني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على قومي وجعل لهم ما أسلموا عليه من أموالهم الحديث وفيه قصة له مع عمر في زكاة العسل قال البغوي لا أعلم له غيره
records.english: al-Dawsī. Ibn Ḥibbān said: He had companionship with the Prophet. Aḥmad and Ibn Abī Shaybah narrated through Busr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, from Saʿd ibn Abī Dhubāb, who said: “I came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and embraced Islam. The Messenger of God ﷺ appointed me over my people and confirmed their possession of the property they held when they embraced Islam.” The hadith also includes an account involving him and ʿUmar concerning the zakāt on honey. Al-Baghawī said: I know of no other hadith from him.

records.arabic: له ذكر في حديث أخرجه أبو داود والنسائي وابن أبي شيبة والدارقطني والحاكم من طريق السدي عن مصعب بن سعد عن أبيه قال لما كان يوم فتح مكة أمن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الناس إلا أربعة أنفس عكرمة بن أبي جهل وعبد الله بن خطل ومقيس بن صبابة وعبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سرح فأما بن خطل فقتل وهو متعلق بأستار الكعبة استبق إليه سعد بن ذؤيب وعمار بن ياسر فكان سعد أشب الرجلين فقتله الحديث ووقع في بعض الروايات وهو عند أبي شيبة والبيهقي سعيد بن حريث بدل سعد بن ذؤيب فالله أعلم
records.english:
he is mentioned in a report transmitted by Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Abī Shaybah, al-Dāraquṭnī, and al-Ḥākim through al-Suddī, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, from his father, who said: “On the day of the conquest of Mecca, the Messenger of God ﷺ granted safety to the people apart from four persons: ʿIkrimah ibn Abī Jahl, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khaṭal, Miqyas ibn Ṣubābah, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ. As for Ibn Khaṭal, he was killed while clinging to the curtains of the Kaʿbah. Saʿd ibn Dhuʾayb and ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir raced towards him; Saʿd was the younger of the two men and killed him.” This is part of the hadith.

In some narrations, including those with Abū Shaybah and al-Bayhaqī, Saʿīd ibn Ḥurayth occurs in place of Saʿd ibn Dhuʾayb. فالله أعلم.

records.arabic: ذكره بن حبان في الصحابة وروى الطبراني من طريق بن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال قال سعد بن أبي رافع دخل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعودني فوضع يده بين ثديي حتى وجدت بردها على فؤادي فقالت لي إنك رجل مفئود إئت الحارث بن كلده الحديث تفرد يونس بن الحجاج عن بن عيينة عن بن أبي نجيح بقوله سعد بن أبي رافع ورواه الحسن بن سفيان عن قتيبة عن بن عيينة فقال قال سعد ولم ينسبه وكذا أخرجه أبو داود وابن منده من رواية بن عيينة وروى بن إسحاق عن إسماعيل بن محمد بن سعد بن أبي وقاص عن أبيه عن جده مثل هذا فأما أن يكون يونس بن الحجاج في قوله بن أبي رافع أو تكون القصة تعددت
records.english:
Ibn Ḥibbān listed him among the Companions. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted through Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, who said: Saʿd ibn Abī Rāfiʿ said, “The Messenger of God ﷺ came in to visit me in my illness. He placed his hand between my breasts until I felt its coolness upon my heart, and said to me, ‘You are a man afflicted in the heart. Go to al-Ḥārith ibn Kaldah ...’”—the report continues.

Editorial note: The verb introducing “said to me” has the feminine form فقالت in the Arabic source. The translation follows the explicitly named speaker in the surrounding report.

Yūnus ibn al-Ḥajjāj alone, transmitting from Ibn ʿUyaynah, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, used the wording “Saʿd ibn Abī Rāfiʿ.” Al-Ḥasan ibn Sufyān transmitted it from Qutaybah, from Ibn ʿUyaynah, with the wording “Saʿd said,” without giving his lineage. Abū Dāwūd and Ibn Mandah likewise included it through Ibn ʿUyaynah. Ibn Isḥāq transmitted a similar account from Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father, from his grandfather. Thus, either Yūnus ibn al-Ḥajjāj [predicate missing] in his saying “ibn Abī Rāfiʿ,” or the incident occurred more than once.

Editorial note: The first alternative lacks a predicate in the Arabic source and also in the consulted 1905–1907 edition. What is predicated of Yūnus cannot be recovered from that sentence.

records.arabic: بن مالك بن امرئ القيس بن مالك الأغر بن ثعلبة بن كعب بن الخزرج الأنصاري الخزرجي أحد نقباء الأنصار تقدم ذكره في ترجمة سعد بن خيثمة وروى البخاري من حديث عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال لما قدمنا إلى المدينة آخى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بيني وبين سعد بن الربيع فقال سعد إني أكثر الأنصار مالا فأقاسمك نصف مالي الحديث وفي الصحيحين من حديث أنس نحوه وقال مالك في الموطأ عن يحيى بن سعيد لما كان يوم أحد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من يأتيني بخبر سعد بن الربيع فقال رجل أنا يا رسول الله فجعل يطوف بين القتلى فلقيه فقال أقرىء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم السلام وأخبره أنني طعنت أثنتي عشرة طعنة وإني أنفذت مقاتلي وأخبر قومك أنهم لا عذر لهم عند الله إن قتل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وواحد منهم حي قال أبو عمر في التمهيد لا أعرفه مسندا وهو محفوظ عند أهل السير وقد ذكره بن إسحاق عن محمد بن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن بن أبي صعصعة المازني قلت وفي الصحيح من حديث أنس ما يشهد لبعضه وحكى بن الأثير أن الرجل الذي ذهب إليه هو أبي بن كعب وروى الطبراني من طريق خارجة بن زيد بن ثابت عن أم سعد بنت سعد بن الربيع أنها دخلت على أبي بكر الصديق فألقى لها ثوبه حتى جلست عليه فدخل عمر فسأله فقال هذه ابنة من هو خير مني ومنك قال ومن هو يا خليفة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال رجل قبض على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تبوأ مقعده من الجنة وبقيت أنا وأنت وروى إسماعيل القاضي في أحكام القرآن من طريق عبد الله بن محمد بن حزم أن عمرة بنت حزم كانت تحت سعد بن الربيع فقتل عنها بأحد وكان له منها ابنة فأتت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تطلب ميراث ابنتها ففيها نزلت يستفتونك في النساء الآية اتفقوا على أنه استشهد بأحد وذكر مقاتل في تفسيره أنه نزل فيه الرجال قوامون على النساء الآية ووصفه بأنه من نقباء الأنصار وكذلك ذكره إسماعيل بن أحمد الضرير في تفسيره لكنه سماه أسعد وذكره في حرف الألف وهو تحريف
records.english:
ibn Mālik ibn Imriʾ al-Qays ibn Mālik al-Agharr ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Kaʿb ibn al-Khazraj al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī, one of the representatives of the Anṣār. He was mentioned earlier in the biography of Saʿd ibn Khaythamah.

Al-Bukhārī transmitted the report of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who said: “When we arrived in Medina, the Prophet ﷺ established brotherhood between me and Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ. Saʿd said, ‘I am the wealthiest of the Anṣār, so I will divide my wealth equally with you ...’”—the report continues. A similar report from Anas appears in the two Ṣaḥīḥs.

Mālik said in the Muwaṭṭaʾ, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd: On the day of Uḥud, the Messenger of God ﷺ said, “Who will bring me news of Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ?” A man said, “I will, Messenger of God.” He went about among the slain until he found him. Saʿd said, “Convey my greetings to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and tell him that I have been stabbed twelve times and that my vital parts have been pierced. Tell your people that they will have no excuse before God if the Messenger of God ﷺ is killed while one of them is still alive.”

Abū ʿUmar said in al-Tamhīd: “I do not know of a version with a connected chain of transmission, but it is preserved among the biographers.” Ibn Isḥāq mentioned it from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ṣaʿṣaʿah al-Māzinī. I say: A report from Anas in the Ṣaḥīḥ corroborates part of it. Ibn al-Athīr related that the man who went to him was Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.

Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted through Khārijah ibn Zayd ibn Thābit, from Umm Saʿd bint Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ, that she entered the presence of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq. He laid down his garment for her, and she sat on it. ʿUmar came in and asked him about this. He said, “This is the daughter of someone better than me and you.” He asked, “Who was he, successor to the Messenger of God ﷺ?” He replied, “A man who died during the lifetime of the Messenger of God ﷺ and took his place in Paradise, while you and I have remained behind.”

Ismāʿīl al-Qāḍī transmitted in Aḥkām al-Qurʾān, through ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥazm, that ʿAmrah bint Ḥazm was married to Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ. He was killed at Uḥud, leaving her a widow, and he had a daughter by her. She came to the Prophet ﷺ seeking her daughter's inheritance. Concerning her, the verse “They ask you for a ruling concerning women ...” was revealed.

They agree that he was martyred at Uḥud. Muqātil mentioned in his commentary that the verse “Men are in charge of women ...” was revealed concerning him, and described him as one of the representatives of the Anṣār. Ismāʿīl ibn Aḥmad al-Ḍarīr likewise mentioned him in his commentary, but called him Asʿad and listed him under the letter alif. This is a corruption.

records.arabic: الأنصاري أبو الحارث ويعرف بسعد بن الحنظلية وهو أخو سهل بن الحنظلية والحنظلية أمهما وقيل جدتهما وقال أبو عمر بن عبد البر قيل أن اسم أبيهما عقيب قلت هو قول بن سعد وقال أبو حاتم استشهد بأحد وفيه نظر ولعله أراد الذي قبله وأما هذا فذكر بن سعد أنه شهد الخندق
records.english:
al-Anṣārī, Abū al-Ḥārith, known as Saʿd ibn al-Ḥanẓaliyyah. He is the brother of Sahl ibn al-Ḥanẓaliyyah. Al-Ḥanẓaliyyah was their mother, or, according to another account, their grandmother. Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: “It has been said that their father's name was ʿAqīb.” I say: That is Ibn Saʿd's statement.

Abū Ḥātim said that he was martyred at Uḥud. This is questionable; perhaps he meant the man in the preceding entry. As for this man, Ibn Saʿd mentioned that he participated in the Battle of the Trench.

names.arabic: سعد بن الربيع بن عمرو بن عدي
names.english: Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAdī

title.arabic: سعد بن الربيع بن عمرو بن عدي
title.english: Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAdī

records.arabic: الأنصاري هو أخو أسعد تقدم نسبه في ترجمة أخيه ذكره أبو حاتم في الصحابة والباوردي وابن شاهين وروينا في الثالث من حديث أبي روق الهمداني من طريق يحيى بن أبي كثير عن محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن ثوبان عن سعد بن زرارة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يدعو اللهم انصرني على من بغى على الحديث وروى الطبراني في ترجمة يونس بن راشد في مسند الشاميين من حديث بن عباس قال لنا نزلت وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه الآية أتى أبو بكر وعمر ومعاذ بن جبل وسعد بن زرارة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا ما نزلت علينا آية أشد من هذه وروى بن منده في ترجمته من طريق أبي الرجال محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن سعد بن زرارة أن أباه حدثه عن جده سعد أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال يوما وهو يحدث عن ربه ما أحب الله من عبده منكر شيء من النعم ما أحب أن أذكره ما هداه له من الايمان الحديث وأخرجه أبو نعيم من هذا الوجه لكن وقع عنده من وجه آخر عن جده أسعد وأسعد وسعد معا جدان لمحمد أحدهما لأبيه والآخر لأمه وهذا الحديث من حديث أسعد ولذلك نسب أبو نعيم الوهم فيه لابن منده لكن قد ذكره غيره في الصحابة قال بن عبد البر فيه نظر وأخشى ألا يكون أدركه الإسلام لأن أكثرهم لم يذكره وقد ذكر الواقدي والعدوي أنه كان ينسب إلى النفاق ولعله تاب والله أعلم
records.english:
al-Anṣārī. He is the brother of Asʿad; his lineage was given earlier in his brother's biography. Abū Ḥātim, al-Bāwardī, and Ibn Shāhīn listed him among the Companions.

We have transmitted, in the third part of the reports of Abū Rawq al-Hamdānī, through Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Thawbān, from Saʿd ibn Zurārah, that the Messenger of God ﷺ used to pray, “O God, grant me victory over whoever wrongs me ...”—the report continues.

Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted in the biography of Yūnus ibn Rāshid in Musnad al-Shāmiyyīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said to us: “The verse ‘Whether you disclose what is within yourselves or conceal it ...’ was revealed. Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, Muʿādh ibn Jabal, and Saʿd ibn Zurārah came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said, ‘No verse harder upon us than this has been revealed.’”

Ibn Mandah transmitted in his biography through Abū al-Rijāl Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿd ibn Zurārah, whose father related to him from his grandfather Saʿd, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said one day while relating from his Lord: “[The Arabic sentence is unclear; the following are provisional fragments:] What God loves from His servant ... a denier of anything among the blessings ... what I love to mention to him ... the faith to which He guided him ...”—the report continues.

Editorial note: The source has منكر in the phrase about blessings; the 1905–1907 edition instead has ذكر. That difference does not establish how the clauses fit together or securely determine who acts on whom in أذكره. The fragments above should not be read as a reconstructed, continuous divine saying.

Abū Nuʿaym included it through this route, but in another route he has “from his grandfather Asʿad.” Asʿad and Saʿd were both grandfathers of Muḥammad, one on his father's side and the other on his mother's. This report is from Asʿad, which is why Abū Nuʿaym attributed the error in it to Ibn Mandah. Others, however, have also listed Saʿd among the Companions.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: “This is questionable. I fear he may not have lived into the time of Islam, since most of them do not mention him.” Al-Wāqidī and al-ʿAdawī mentioned that hypocrisy was attributed to him. Perhaps he repented. والله أعلم.

names.arabic: محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن ثوبان
names.english: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Thawbān

names.arabic: أبي الرجال محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن سعد بن زرارة
names.english: Abū al-Rijāl Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿd ibn Zurārah

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الأشهلي قال أبو حاتم له صحبه وروى البخاري في التاريخ والحاكم وابن منه من طريق إبراهيم بن جعفر من ولد محمد بن مسلمة عن سليمان بن محمد بن محمود بن مسلمة عن سعد الأشهلي أنه أهدى إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سيفا الحديث قال البغوي لا أعلم له غيره وأخرجه بن منده والطبراني في الأوسط من وجه آخر فجاء فيه سعيد بزيادة ياء والأول أرجح
records.english:
al-Ashhalī. Abū Ḥātim said that he was a Companion. Al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh, al-Ḥākim, and [Ibn Mandah] transmitted through Ibrāhīm ibn Jaʿfar, a descendant of Muḥammad ibn Maslamah, from Sulaymān ibn Muḥammad ibn Maḥmūd ibn Maslamah, from Saʿd al-Ashhalī, that he presented a sword to the Messenger of God ﷺ—the report continues.

Editorial note: The third compiler is written ابن منه in the Arabic source. The bracketed identification as Ibn Mandah follows the explicit reading ابن منده in this same compiler list in the 1905–1907 edition; it does not change the Arabic source.

Al-Baghawī said, “I know of no other report from him.” Ibn Mandah and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ included it through another route, where the name appears as Saʿīd, with an additional yāʾ. The first reading is more likely.

names.arabic: سليمان بن محمد بن محمود بن مسلمة
names.english: Sulaymān ibn Muḥammad ibn Maḥmūd ibn Maslamah

records.arabic: تقدم في أسعد
records.english: was previously mentioned under Asʿad.

records.arabic:
بن عبد بن كعب بن عبد الأشهل الأنصاري الأشهلي ذكره موسى بن عقبة وابن إسحاق وغيرهما فيمن شهد بدرا وقال الواقدي شهد العقبة وزعم أبو عمر والعسكري وأبو نعيم أنه راوي الحديث المتقدم قبل ترجمة وهو وهم فإن اسم ذاك سعد وليس في نسب هذا من اسمه سعد وله ذكر في السيرة وأنه الذي هدم المنار الذي كان بالمشلل وأنه الذي بعثه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بسبايا من بني قريظة فاشترى بها من نجد خيلا وسلاحا وفي ديوان حسان بن ثابت لما أغار عيينة بن حصن على سرح المدينة قال حسان في ذلك
هل سر أولاد اللقيطة أننا
سلم غداة فوارس المقداد قال فعاتبه سعد بن زيد الأشهلي لأنه كان الرئيس يومئذ كيف نسب الفوارس للمقداد ولم ينسبها إلي فاعتذر إليه بالقافية وأراد باللقيطة أم حصن بن حذيفة
records.english:
ibn ʿAbd ibn Kaʿb ibn ʿAbd al-Ashhal al-Anṣārī al-Ashhalī. Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, Ibn Isḥāq, and others listed him among those who participated at Badr. Al-Wāqidī said that he attended al-ʿAqabah.

Abū ʿUmar, al-ʿAskarī, and Abū Nuʿaym claimed that he was the narrator of the report mentioned two entries earlier. This is an error, for that one's name is Saʿd, whereas no one in this man's ancestry is named Saʿd.

Editorial note: The intended contrast in the preceding sentence is unclear. The Arabic source and the 1905–1907 edition both compare the name Saʿd with its absence from the present man's ancestry, without specifying a different ancestral relationship. No such relationship has been supplied in the translation.

He is mentioned in the biography of the Prophet as the man who demolished the marker at al-Mushallal, and as the man whom the Prophet ﷺ sent with captives from Banū Qurayẓah. With them, he bought horses and weapons from Najd.

In the Dīwān of Ḥassān ibn Thābit, when ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn raided Medina's grazing livestock, Ḥassān said about this:

Were the foundling woman's sons pleased that we
were at peace [reading uncertain] on the morning of al-Miqdād's horsemen?

Editorial note: “At peace” is a provisional rendering of سلم. The consulted 1905–1907 edition has the same unvocalized word and following phrase; it does not settle the verse's sense or the precise connection with the morning and the horsemen.

The account says that Saʿd ibn Zayd al-Ashhalī reproached him, since he was the commander that day: “How could he attribute the horsemen to al-Miqdād and not to me?” He offered the rhyme as his excuse. By “the foundling woman,” he meant the mother of Ḥiṣn ibn Ḥudhayfah.

names.english: the mother of Ḥiṣn ibn Ḥudhayfah

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: فرق البغوي بينه وبين الذي قبله وأخرج من طريق يزيد بن أبي زياد عن يزيد بن أبي الحسن عن سعد بن زيد الأنصاري أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حمل حسنا ثم قال اللهم إني أحبه فأحبه مرتين قال البغوي اختلف فيه على يزيد بن أبي زياد
records.english: Al-Baghawī distinguished him from the preceding person. He transmitted through Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from Yazīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan, from Saʿd ibn Zayd al-Anṣārī, that the Prophet ﷺ picked up Ḥasan and then said, “O God, I love him, so love him,” twice. Al-Baghawī said: “The transmissions from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād differ on this.”

records.arabic: في ترجمة زيد بن كعب
records.english: under the biography of Zayd ibn Kaʿb.

title.arabic: سعد بن زيد الطائي أو الأنصاري
title.english: Saʿd ibn Zayd al-Ṭāʾī, or al-Anṣārī

records.arabic: الساعدي اخو سهل بن سعد روى الطبراني من طريق عبد المهيمن بن العباس بن سهل عن أبيه عن جده أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ضرب لسعد بن سعد يوم بدر بسهم والمشهور أن ذلك إنما وقع لسعد والد سهل كما سيأتي في ترجمته وقد قيل إنه سعد بن سعد فإن يكن كذلك سقطت هذه الترجمة لكن المعروف أنه سعد بن مالك كما سيأتي
records.english:
al-Sāʿidī, the brother of Sahl ibn Saʿd. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted through ʿAbd al-Muhaymin ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn Sahl, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Prophet ﷺ allocated Saʿd ibn Saʿd a share on the day of Badr.

The well-known account is that this happened to Saʿd, Sahl's father, as will appear in his biography. It has also been said that his name was Saʿd ibn Saʿd. If that is so, this separate biography falls away. But the known name is Saʿd ibn Mālik, as will appear.

names.arabic: عبد المهيمن بن العباس بن سهل
names.english: ʿAbd al-Muhaymin ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn Sahl

records.arabic: بن سعد الأنصاري حليف بني نوفل قال الطبري وغيره شهد أحدا واستدركه أبو موسى
records.english: ibn Saʿd, al-Anṣārī, an ally of Banū Nawfal. Al-Ṭabarī and others said that he participated at Uḥud. Abū Mūsā added him in his supplement.

records.arabic: زوج الجهنية يأتي ذكره في باب هند من النساء إن شاء الله تعالى
records.english: the husband of the Juhanī woman. He will be mentioned under Hind in the section on women, إن شاء الله تعالى.

records.arabic: بن مالك بن حبيب بن مالك بن خفاف السلمي قال الرشاطي ذكر في الشجرة البغدادية في النسب أنه وفد على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
records.english: ibn Mālik ibn Ḥabīb ibn Mālik ibn Khufāf al-Sulamī. Al-Rushāṭī said: “It is mentioned in al-Shajarah al-Baghdādiyyah, on genealogy, that he came as a delegate to the Messenger of God ﷺ.”

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن وقش الأشهلي قال بن الكلبي استشهد يوم الجسر مع أبي عبيد وقد قيل هو اسم أبي نائلة وقد فرق بينهما بن الكلبي والصواب أن اسم أبي نائلة ملكان ويأتي في الكنى
records.english: ibn Waqsh, al-Ashhalī. Ibn al-Kalbī said that he was martyred on the day of the Bridge with Abū ʿUbayd. It has been said that this was the name of Abū Nāʾilah, but Ibn al-Kalbī distinguished the two. The correct name of Abū Nāʾilah is Milkān. He will appear in the section on kunyas.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن قيس أو عبيد بن الأبحر بن خدرة بن عوف بن الحارث بن خزرج الأنصاري الخزرجي ذكره موسى بن عقبة وابن إسحاق فيمن شهد بدرا وذكره بن شهاب فيمن استشهد بأحد وهو الذي سمى جده عبيدا
records.english: ibn Qays, or ʿUbayd, ibn al-Abḥar ibn Khudrah ibn ʿAwf ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Khazraj al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī. Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah and Ibn Isḥāq listed him among those who participated at Badr. Ibn Shihāb listed him among those martyred at Uḥud; it was he who named his grandfather ʿUbayd.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن مالك بن كعب بن عبد الأشهل بن حارثة بن دينار بن النجار الأنصاري الخزرجي ذكره بن عقبة وابن إسحاق فيمن شهد بدرا وسمى أبو الأسود عن عروة أباه سهيلا بالتصغير فجعله بن منده بهذا السبب ترجمتين وقال أبو معشر والواقدي سعيد بن سهيل فجعله أبو موسى ثالثا وذكره بن أبي حاتم عن أبيه فين اسمه سعيد بالتصغير فجعله بن عبد البر وزعم أن بن إسحاق أغفله وليس كذلك
records.english:
ibn Mālik ibn Kaʿb ibn ʿAbd al-Ashhal ibn Ḥārithah ibn Dīnār ibn al-Najjār al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī.

Editorial note: The final classification clause is incomplete in the Arabic base. The bracketed completion below follows the 1905–1907 edition (vol. 2, p. 79, entry 3161), which treats him as a separate person but does not name Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr in that clause. The attribution to Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr is retained from the base; that difference between the editions remains.

Ibn ʿUqbah and Ibn Isḥāq listed him among those who fought at Badr. Abū al-Aswad, reporting from ʿUrwah, named his father Suhayl, in the diminutive form; on this account Ibn Mandah made two biographical entries for him. Abū Maʿshar and al-Wāqidī called him Saʿīd ibn Suhayl, so Abū Mūsā made a third entry. Ibn Abī Ḥātim mentioned him on his father's authority among those whose name was Suʿayd, in the diminutive form. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr consequently treated him [as a separate person] and asserted that Ibn Isḥāq had omitted him; that is not so.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن سعد بن سفيان بن مالك بن حبيب بن زعب بن مالك بن خفاف بن امرئ القيس بن بهثة بن سليم السلمي وقيل الأسلمي وقيل فيه الضمري حجازي شهد حنينا ساق نسبه بن قانع له عند أبي داود حديث في قصة محلم بن جثامة بإسناد حسن وسيأتي ذكره في ترجمة مكيتل إن شاء الله تعالى
records.english: ibn Saʿd ibn Sufyān ibn Mālik ibn Ḥabīb ibn Zaʿb ibn Mālik ibn Khufāf ibn Imriʾ al-Qays ibn Buhthah ibn Sulaym al-Sulamī; also called al-Aslamī, and al-Ḍumrī is another form given for him. He was from the Hijaz and fought at Ḥunayn. Ibn Qāniʿ set out his lineage. Abū Dāwūd has a report from him about the incident involving Muḥallim ibn Jaththāmah, with a good chain of transmission. He will be mentioned in the biography of Mukaytil, إن شاء الله تعالى.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره الخطيب في المتفق وقال يقال أن له صحبة وفي المسند عدة من المجهولين ثم روى من طريق سهل بن عبيد الواسطي عن يوسف بن زياد عن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن عن سعد بن طريف قال بينا أنا أمشي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في ناحية المدينة وامرأة على حمار يطوف بها أسود في يوم طس إذ أتت يد الحمار على وهده فزلق فصرعت المرأة فصرف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بصره فقلت يا رسول الله إنها متسرولة فقال يرحم الله المتسرولات قال الخطيب لم أكتبه إلا من هذا الوجه وفي إسناده غير واحد من المجهولين وقال بن الجوزي يحتمل أن يكون هو سعد بن طريف الإسكان فسقط شيخه وشيخ شيخه كذا قال
records.english:
Al-Khaṭīb mentioned him in al-Muttafiq and said, "He is said to have been a Companion, and the musnad contains several unknown transmitters."

Editorial note: The description of the day is written طس in both the Arabic base and the 1905–1907 edition (vol. 2, p. 79, entry 3163); its meaning remains uncertain. In the closing quotation, the base has the designation الإسكان, while that edition reads الاسكاف. The English uses the latter reading, al-Iskāf, as an explicit editorial correction; the Arabic base is unchanged.

He then transmitted, through Sahl ibn ʿUbayd al-Wāsiṭī, from Yūsuf ibn Ziyād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf, who said:

"While I was walking with the Prophet ﷺ in an outlying part of Medina, there was a woman on a donkey, with a Black man taking her around, on a day described as طس [meaning uncertain]. The donkey's foreleg came upon a hollow, and it slipped, throwing the woman. The Prophet ﷺ turned his gaze away. I said, ‘Messenger of God, she is wearing trousers.’ He said, ‘May God have mercy on women who wear trousers.’"

Al-Khaṭīb said, "I have recorded it only through this route, and its chain includes more than one unknown transmitter." Ibn al-Jawzī said, "It may be Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf al-Iskāf [editorial reading], with his teacher and his teacher's teacher having dropped out." That is what he said.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن مالك الأنصاري شهد هو وأخوه حمزة أحدا قاله بن سعد والعدوي والطبرى
records.english: ibn Mālik, al-Anṣārī. He and his brother Ḥamzah fought at Uḥud, as stated by Ibn Saʿd, al-ʿAdawī, and al-Ṭabarī.

records.arabic: المؤذن مولى عمار بن ياسر وقيل مولى الأنصار ويقال اسم أبيه عبد الرحمن كان يتجر بالقرظ فقيل له سعد القرظ وروى البغوي عن القاسم بن محمد بن عمر بن حفص بن عمر بن سعد القرظ عن آبائه أن سعدا اشتكي إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قلة ذات يده فأمره بالتجارة فخرج إلى السوق فاشترى شيئا من قرظ فباعه فربح فيه فذكر ذلك للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأمره بلزوم ذلك وروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأذن في حياته بمسجد قباء روى عنه ابناه عمار وعمر نقلة أبو بكر من قباء إلى المسجد النبوي فأذن فيه بعد بلال وتوارث عنه بنوه الأذان قال خليفة أذن سعد لأبي بكر ولعمر بعده وروى يونس عن الزهري أن الذي نقله عن قباء عمر قال أبو أحمد العسكري عاش سعد القرظ إلى أيام الحجاج
records.english:
the muezzin, the client of ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir; alternatively, a client of the Anṣār. His father's name is also said to have been ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. He traded in qaraẓ, an acacia tanning material, and was therefore called Saʿd al-Qaraẓ.

Al-Baghawī transmitted from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar ibn Saʿd al-Qaraẓ, from his forefathers, that Saʿd complained to the Prophet ﷺ of his lack of means. He instructed him to engage in trade. Saʿd went out to the market, bought some qaraẓ, and sold it at a profit. He mentioned this to the Prophet ﷺ, who instructed him to keep to that trade.

He narrated from the Prophet ﷺ and called the prayer at the mosque of Qubāʾ during his lifetime. His two sons, ʿAmmār and ʿUmar, narrated from him. Abū Bakr transferred him from Qubāʾ to the Prophet's Mosque, where he called the prayer after Bilāl. His descendants inherited the calling of the prayer from him. Khalīfah said, "Saʿd called the prayer for Abū Bakr and for ʿUmar after him." Yūnus transmitted from al-Zuhrī that it was ʿUmar who transferred him from Qubāʾ. Abū Aḥmad al-ʿAskarī said, "Saʿd al-Qaraẓ lived until the days of al-Ḥajjāj."

names.english: al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar ibn Saʿd al-Qaraẓ

In al-Bukhārī's Tārīkh there is a Saʿd ibn ʿAbbād al-Zuraqī who narrated from ʿUmar, and from whom his son ʿUmar narrated. He may be this man.

records.arabic: بن دليم بن حارثة بن حرام بن خزيمة بن ثعلبة بن طريف بن الخزرج بن ساعدة بن كعب بن الخزرج الأنصاري سيد الخزرج يكنى أبا ثابت وأبا قيس وأمه عمرة بنت مسعود لها صحبة وماتت في زمن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سنة خمس وشهد سعد العقبة وكان أحد النقباء واختلف في شهوده بدرا فأثبته البخاري وقال بن سعد كان يتهيأ للخروج فنهس فأقام وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لقد كان حريصا عليها قال بن سعد وكان يكتب بالعربية ويحسن العوم والرمي فكان يقال له الكامل وكان مشهورا بالجود هو وأبوه وجده وولده وكان لهم أطم ينادي عليه كل يوم من أحب الشحم واللحم فليأت أطم دليم بن حارثة وكانت جفنة سعد تدور مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في بيوت أزواجه وقال مقسم عن بن عباس كان لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في المواطن كلها رايتان مع علي راية المهاجرين ومع سعد بن عبادة راية الأنصار وروى له أحمد من طريق محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن سعد بن زرارة عن قيس بن سعد زارنا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في منزلنا فقال السلام عليكم ورحمة الله الحديث وفيه ثم رفع يده فقال اللهم اجعل صلواتك ورحمتك على آل سعد بن عبادة وروى أبو يعلى من حديث جابر قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جزى الله عنا الأنصار خيرا لا سيما عبد الله بن عمرو بن حرام وسعد بن عبادة وروى بن أبي الدنيا من طريق بن سيرين قال كان أهل الصفة إذا أمسوا انطلق الرجل بالواحد والرجل بالاثنين والرجل بالجماعة فأما سعد فكان ينطلق بثمانين وروى الدارقطني في كتاب الأسخياء من طريق هشام بن عروة عن أبيه قال كان منادي سعد ينادي على أطمة من كان يريد شحما ولحما فليأت سعدا وكان سعد يقول اللهم هب لي مجدا لا مجد إلا بفعال ولا فعال إلا بمال اللهم إنه لا يصلحنى القليل ولا أصلح عليه وعن محمد بن سيرين كان سعد بن عبادة يعشى كل ليلة ثمانين من أهل الصفة وقصته في تخلفه عن بيعة أبي بكر مشهورة وخرج إلى الشام فمات بحوران سنة خمس عشرة وقيل سنة ست عشرة وروى عنه بنوه قيس وسعيد وإسحاق وحفيده شرحبيل بن سعيد وروى عنه من الصحابة أيضا بن عباس وأبو أمامة بن سهل وأرسل عنه الحسن وعيسى بن فائد وروى أبو داود من حديث قيس بن سعد أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال اللهم اجعل صلواتك ورحمتك على آل سعد بن عبادة أخرجه في أثناء حديث وقيل إن قبره بالمنيحة قرية بدمشق بالغوطة وعن سعد عيد بن عبد العزيز أنه مات ببصرى وهي أول مدينة فتحت من الشام
records.english:
ibn Dulaym ibn Ḥārithah ibn Ḥarām ibn Khuzaymah ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Ṭarīf ibn al-Khazraj ibn Sāʿidah ibn Kaʿb ibn al-Khazraj al-Anṣārī, chief of the Khazraj. His kunyahs were Abū Thābit and Abū Qays. His mother, ʿAmrah bint Masʿūd, was a Companion; she died during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, in the year 5.

Editorial note: The authority named in the final death report is damaged in the Arabic base, which reads سعد عيد بن عبد العزيز. The 1905–1907 edition (vol. 2, pp. 80–81, entry 3167) reads سعيد بن عبد العزيز. The English uses Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz as a disclosed editorial reading; the Arabic base and the differing death and burial reports remain unchanged.

Saʿd attended al-ʿAqabah and was one of the representatives. There is disagreement about his participation at Badr; al-Bukhārī affirmed it. Ibn Saʿd said, "He was preparing to set out, but was bitten and stayed behind." The Prophet ﷺ said, "He had certainly been eager to take part in it."

Ibn Saʿd said, "He could write Arabic and was skilled at swimming and archery, so he was called al-Kāmil, ‘the accomplished man.’" He, his father, his grandfather, and his children were renowned for generosity. They had a fortified tower, from which a proclamation went out each day: "Let anyone who wants fat and meat come to the tower of Dulaym ibn Ḥārithah." Saʿd's large food bowl went with the Prophet ﷺ from one wife's house to another.

Miqsam reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, "At every engagement the Messenger of God ﷺ had two banners: ʿAlī carried the banner of the Emigrants, and Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah carried the banner of the Anṣār."

Aḥmad transmitted a report concerning him through Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿd ibn Zurārah, from Qays ibn Saʿd: "The Prophet ﷺ visited us at our home and said, ‘Peace be upon you, and God's mercy.’" The report continues, and includes: "Then he raised his hand and said, ‘O God, bestow Your blessings and Your mercy upon the family of Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah.’"

Abū Yaʿlā transmitted from Jābir, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said, "May God reward the Anṣār with good on our behalf, especially ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥarām and Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah."

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā transmitted through Ibn Sīrīn, who said, "When evening came upon the people of the Ṣuffah, one man would take one of them with him, another two, and another a group. Saʿd would take eighty."

Al-Dāraquṭnī transmitted in his Kitāb al-Askhiyāʾ, through Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father: "Saʿd's herald would call out from his fortified tower, ‘Let anyone who wants fat and meat come to Saʿd.’ Saʿd used to say, ‘O God, grant me honor. There is no honor without deeds, and no deeds without wealth. O God, little does not serve me well, nor do I fare well with it.’"

It is reported from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn that Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah provided an evening meal every night for eighty of the people of the Ṣuffah. The account of his refraining from pledging allegiance to Abū Bakr is well known. He went to al-Shām and died in Ḥawrān in the year 15; the year 16 is also given.

His sons Qays, Saʿīd, and Isḥāq narrated from him, as did his grandson Shuraḥbīl ibn Saʿīd. Among the Companions, Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Umāmah ibn Sahl also narrated from him. Al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā ibn Fāʾid transmitted reports from him with a gap in the chain.

Abū Dāwūd transmitted from Qays ibn Saʿd that the Prophet ﷺ said, "O God, bestow Your blessings and Your mercy upon the family of Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah." He included this within a longer hadith.

His grave is said to be at al-Manīḥah, a village in the Ghūṭah of Damascus. It is reported from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz [editorial reading] that he died at Buṣrā, the first city in al-Shām to be conquered.

records.arabic: روى بن مردويه في التفسير من طريق يعلى بن الأشدق حدثنا سعد بن عبد الله أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عن قوله تعالى إن الذين ينادونك من وراء الحجرات الآية قال هم الجفاة من بني تميم لولا أنهم من أشد الناس قتالا للاعور الدجال لدعوت الله أن يهلكهم قال بن منده غريب لا نعرفه إلا من هذا الوجه قلت ويعلى متروك الحديث
records.english:
Ibn Mardawayh related in his Tafsīr, through Yaʿlā ibn al-Ashdaq: "Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us that the Prophet ﷺ was asked about the saying of God تعالى, ‘Indeed, those who call you from beyond the chambers’—the verse. He said, ‘They are the coarse people of Banū Tamīm. Were they not among the fiercest fighters against the one-eyed Dajjāl, I would ask God to destroy them.’"

Ibn Mandah said, "It is an isolated report; we know it only through this route." I say: Yaʿlā is rejected as a hadith transmitter.

records.arabic: بن النعمان بن قيس بن عمرو بن زيد بن أمية بن زيد الأنصاري الأوسي ذكره موسى بن عقبة وغيره فيمن شهد بدرا وقال بن نمير في تاريخه مات سعد بن عبيد القاري بالقادسية شهيدا سنة ست عشرة وهو أبو زيد الذي جمع القرآن وروى الزبير بن بكار في أخبار المدينة عن عتبة بن عويم بن ساعدة أن سعد بن عبيد وساق نسبه كان يؤم في مسجد قباء في زمن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبي بكر وعمر وتوفي في زمنه فأمر عمر مجمع بن جارية أن يصلي بهم وروى البخاري في تاريخه من طريق قيس بن مسلم عن طارق بن شهاب قال شهد سعد بن عبيد القادسية فقام خطيبا فقال إنا مستشهدون غدا فلا تكفنونا إلا في ثيابنا التي أصبنا فيها الحديث وروى بن جرير من طريق قيس بن مسلم عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى قال قال عمر لسعد بن عبيد وكان انهزم يوم أصيب أبو عبيد وكان يسمى القارئ ولم يكن أحد يسمى القارئ غيره فذكر قصته قلت اختلف في أبي زيد الذي جمع القرآن في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقيل هذا اسمه وقيل بل اسمه سعيد وقيل غير ذلك
records.english:
ibn al-Nuʿmān ibn Qays ibn ʿAmr ibn Zayd ibn Umayyah ibn Zayd al-Anṣārī al-Awsī. Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah and others listed him among those who fought at Badr. Ibn Numayr said in his Tārīkh, "Saʿd ibn ʿUbayd the reciter died as a martyr at al-Qādisiyyah in the year 16. He is Abū Zayd, who collected the Qurʾān."

Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār transmitted in Akhbār al-Madīnah, from ʿUtbah ibn ʿUwaym ibn Sāʿidah, that Saʿd ibn ʿUbayd—he set out his lineage—used to lead the prayer in the mosque of Qubāʾ during the times of the Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar. He died during ʿUmar's time, so ʿUmar instructed Mujammiʿ ibn Jāriyah to lead them in prayer.

Al-Bukhārī transmitted in his Tārīkh, through Qays ibn Muslim, from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb, who said, "Saʿd ibn ʿUbayd fought at al-Qādisiyyah. He stood to address the people and said, ‘We shall be martyred tomorrow, so shroud us only in the clothes in which we are struck down.’" The report continues.

Ibn Jarīr transmitted through Qays ibn Muslim, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, who said, "ʿUmar addressed Saʿd ibn ʿUbayd, who had fled on the day Abū ʿUbayd was struck down. He was called ‘the reciter,’ and no one other than him was called ‘the reciter.’" He then related his story.

I say: There is disagreement about Abū Zayd, who collected the Qurʾān during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ. This was said to be his name, but it was also said that his name was Saʿīd, and other names have been given.

records.arabic: بن خلدة بن مخلد بن عامر بن زريق الأنصاري الزرقي أبو عبادة ذكره موسى بن عقبة وغيره في البدريين روى الزبير بن بكار في أخبار المدينة من طريق محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن سعد أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أتى بئر إهاب بالحرة وهي يومئذ لسعد بن عثمان قد ترك عليها ابنه عبادة يسقي فلم يعرفه عبادة ثم جاء سعد فوصفه له فقال ذلك رسول الله الحق به فلحقه فمسح رأسه ودعا له يقال مات وهو بن ثمانين سنة وما شاب
records.english:
ibn Khaldah ibn Makhlad ibn ʿĀmir ibn Zurayq al-Anṣārī al-Zuraqī, Abū ʿUbādah. Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah and others listed him among the men of Badr.

Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār transmitted in Akhbār al-Madīnah, through Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿd, that the Prophet ﷺ came to the well of Ihāb at al-Ḥarrah. At the time it belonged to Saʿd ibn ʿUthmān, who had left his son ʿUbādah there to provide water. ʿUbādah did not recognize him. When Saʿd arrived, ʿUbādah described him to his father, who said, "That was the Messenger of God. Catch up with him." He caught up with him, and the Prophet stroked his head and prayed for him. It is said that ʿUbādah died at the age of eighty without having gone gray.

records.arabic: قال عمر بن شبة حدثنا أبو نعيم حدثنا أبو بكر بن عياش قال جاء رجل من بني ثعلبة بن سعد يقال له سعد بن عمارة فقال يا رسول الله ما تكلمت بكلمة قط إلا مخطومة مزمومة وذكر سيف في الفتوح أن خالد بن الوليد استعمل سعد بن عمارة فيمن استعمل من كماة الصحابة على غطفان وروى الطبراني من طريق بن إسحاق عن عبد الله بن أبي بكر بن حزم وغيره عن سعد بن عمارة أحد بني سعد بن بكر وكانت له صحبة أن رجلا قال له عظنى قال إذا قمت إلى الصلاة فصل صلاة مودع وانظر إلى ما تعتذرى عنه من القول والفعل فاجتنبه وأخرجه البخاري في تاريخه من طريقين إلى بن إسحاق في أحدهما أنه سعد وفي الآخر أنه سعيد ورجح أنه سعد وكذا أخرجه أحمد في كتاب الإيمان والطبراني ورجاله ثقات وأخرجه أبو نعيم من طريق إسماعيل بن محمد بن سعد الأنصاري عن أبيه عن جده فذكره مرفوعا لكنه أفرده بترجمة فقال سعد أبو محمد وذكر هذا الحديث والذي يظهر أنه هو
records.english:
ʿUmar ibn Shabbah said: "Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, saying, ‘A man of Banū Thaʿlabah ibn Saʿd called Saʿd ibn ʿUmārah came and said, “Messenger of God, not a word have I [or: you] ever spoken except haltered and bridled.”’"

Editorial note: The Arabic تكلمت in the opening quotation can mean either “I spoke” or “you spoke.” The 1905–1907 edition (vol. 2, p. 81, entry 3174) has the same form without a distinguishing vowel. Both possibilities are retained; the statement may concern Saʿd’s speech or address the Messenger’s speech.

Sayf mentioned in al-Futūḥ that Khālid ibn al-Walīd appointed Saʿd ibn ʿUmārah over Ghaṭafān, among the valiant Companions whom he appointed.

Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted through Ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn Ḥazm and others, from Saʿd ibn ʿUmārah, a man of Banū Saʿd ibn Bakr who had been a Companion, that a man said to him, "Give me counsel." He replied, "When you stand to pray, pray as one bidding farewell. Consider what words and deeds you would have to apologize for, and avoid them."

Al-Bukhārī included it in his Tārīkh through two routes to Ibn Isḥāq. In one he is Saʿd, and in the other Saʿīd; he considered Saʿd the more likely form. Aḥmad also included it in his Kitāb al-Īmān, as did al-Ṭabarānī, and its transmitters are trustworthy.

Abū Nuʿaym transmitted it through Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿd al-Anṣārī, from his father, from his grandfather, relating it as a saying attributed to the Prophet. He nevertheless gave him a separate biography, under "Saʿd, Abū Muḥammad," and cited this hadith. It appears that he is the same man.

names.arabic: عبد الله بن أبي بكر بن حزم
names.english: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn Ḥazm

names.arabic: إسماعيل بن محمد بن سعد الأنصاري
names.english: Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿd al-Anṣārī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: وقيل عمارة بن سعد قيل هو اسم أبي سعيد الزرقي ويأتي في الكنى
records.english: also said to be ʿUmārah ibn Saʿd. This is said to be the name of Abū Saʿīd al-Zuraqī. He will appear in the section on kunyahs.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن مبذول الأنصاري تقدم ذكره في ترجمة أخيه حمزة
records.english: ibn Mabdhūl, al-Anṣārī. He was mentioned earlier in the biography of his brother Ḥamza.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن مالك بن مبذول بن النجار الأنصاري ذكروه فيمن شهد أحدا واستشهد هو وابنه الطفيل وابن أخيه سهل بن عامر بن عمرو بن ثقف ببئر معونة
records.english: ibn Mālik ibn Mabdhūl ibn al-Najjār al-Anṣārī. They listed him among those who fought at Uḥud. He, his son al-Ṭufayl, and his nephew Sahl ibn ʿĀmir ibn ʿAmr ibn Thaqf were martyred at Biʾr Maʿūna.

aliases: Sahl ibn ʿĀmir ibn ʿAmr ibn Thaqf

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: تقدم ذكره ونسبه في ترجمه أخيه الحارث وليس أبوهما جد جابر بن عبد الله بل توافقا والنسب مختلف وذكر أبو إسماعيل الأزدي في فتوح الشام أن خالد بن الوليد استخلفه بالأنبار لما رحل من العراق إلى الشام ويأتي له ذكر في ترجمة سويد بن قطبة في القسم الثالث
records.english: He and his lineage were mentioned earlier in the biography of his brother al-Ḥārith. Their father was not the grandfather of Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh: the names merely coincide, while the lineages differ. Abū Ismāʿīl al-Azdī stated in Futūḥ al-Shām that Khālid ibn al-Walīd left him in charge at al-Anbār when he departed from Iraq for Syria. He will also be mentioned in the biography of Suwayd ibn Quṭba in the third division.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن الحارث بن كعب بن معاوية بن عمرو بن مالك بن النجار الأنصاري ذكر العدوي أنه شهد أحدا واستشهد باليمامة واستدركه بن الدباغ وابن فتحون وتبعهما بن الكلبي كما سبق
records.english: ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb ibn Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAmr ibn Mālik ibn al-Najjār al-Anṣārī. Al-ʿAdawī stated that he fought at Uḥud and was martyred at al-Yamāma. Ibn al-Dabbāgh and Ibn Fatḥūn added him to their supplements, and Ibn al-Kalbī followed them, as noted earlier.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الأنصاري أخو الحارث بن عمرو كانا ممن شهد صفين من الصحابة قاله أبو عمر ونقله بن الكلبي كما تقدم في ترجمة الحارث بن عمرو قلت لعله الذي قبله فقد جزم بن فتحون بأنهما واحد
records.english: al-Anṣārī, the brother of al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAmr. Both were among the Companions who fought at Ṣiffīn. Abū ʿUmar said this, and Ibn al-Kalbī transmitted it, as noted earlier in the biography of al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAmr. I say: Perhaps he is the man in the preceding notice, for Ibn Fatḥūn stated categorically that the two were one man.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الثقفي ذكره خليفة بن خياط فيمن نزل البصرة من الصحابة
records.english: al-Thaqafī. Khalīfah ibn Khayyāṭ mentioned him among the Companions who settled in Basra.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: قال بن منده حديثه عند عمرو بن قيس عن محمد بن جحادة عن أبيه عنه وقيل فيه عمير بن سعد
records.english: Ibn Mandah said: His report is transmitted by ʿAmr ibn Qays, from Muḥammad ibn Juḥāda, from his father, from him. His name is also given as ʿUmayr ibn Saʿd.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن زيد الأنصاري ويقال سعيد بن زيد بن الفاكه ويقال في أبيه يزيد قال أبو نعيم ذكره بن إسحاق فيمن شهد بدرا قلت وقد تقدم في الألف أسعد بن الفاكه فإن لم يكن هذا أخاه وإلا فهذا تصحيف والذي في المغازي لابن إسحاق ما نصه وشهدها من بني عامر بن زريق سعد بن الفاكه بن زيد بن خلدة بن عامر فهذا هو المعتمد
records.english:
ibn Zayd, al-Anṣārī. He is also called Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn al-Fākih, and his father's name is also given as Yazīd. Abū Nuʿaym said: Ibn Isḥāq listed him among those who fought at Badr. I say: Asʿad ibn al-Fākih was mentioned earlier under alif. If this man was not his brother—otherwise, this is a scribal misreading.

Editorial note: The Arabic reads فإن لم يكن هذا أخاه وإلا فهذا تصحيف. It joins a negative condition to “otherwise” without a clear connecting consequence. The 1905–1907 alternative edition has the same construction. The relation between the brotherhood condition and the diagnosis of a scribal misreading remains uncertain.

The wording in Ibn Isḥāq's al-Maghāzī is: ‘Among Banū ʿĀmir ibn Zurayq, Saʿd ibn al-Fākih ibn Zayd ibn Khalda ibn ʿĀmir fought there.’ This, then, is the form to rely upon.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: قال بن أبي شيبة حدثنا عبد الوهاب الثقفي عن أيوب أن سعد بن قرحاء رجل من الصحابة جمع بين امرأة رجل وابنته من غيرها وقد مضى مثل هذا في جبلة من حرف الجيم
records.english: Ibn Abī Shaybah said: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Thaqafī related to us, from Ayyūb, that Saʿd ibn Qarḥāʾ, a man among the Companions, was married simultaneously to a man's wife and that man's daughter by another woman. A similar account appeared earlier under Jabala in the letter jīm.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: العنزي وقيل العنسي روى بن منده من طريق ضمرة بن مروان بن عبد الله بن حكيم بن عبد الله بن سعد بن قيسي حدثني أبي عن جدي عن أبيه عبد الله عن أبيه سعد بن قيس أنه قدم على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال له ما اسمك قال سعد الخيل قال بل أنت سعد الخير ومن طريق يحيى بن سعيد الأنصاري عن عبد الله بن أبي سلمة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث سعد بن مالك وسعد الخير إلى مكة وروى بن قانع وابن منده من طريق الحسن بن فرقد عن الحسن عن سعد بن قيس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال قال الله يا بن آدم صل أربع ركعات أول النهار أكفك آخره وغاير بن منده بين صاحب الإسناد الأول وبين الذي روى عنه الحسن مع قوله في الأول روى عنه ابنه عبد الله والحسن
records.english:
al-ʿAnazī, also said to be al-ʿAnsī. Ibn Mandah transmitted through Ḍamra ibn Marwān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥakīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Qaysī: My father related to me, from my grandfather, from his father ʿAbd Allāh, from his father Saʿd ibn Qays, that he came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. He asked him, ‘What is your name?’ He replied, ‘Saʿd al-Khayl.’ He said, ‘Rather, you are Saʿd al-Khayr.’ Through Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Salama, it is reported that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم sent Saʿd ibn Mālik and Saʿd al-Khayr to Mecca.

Editorial note: The first genealogy is written قيسي, rendered here as Qaysī, whereas the later chain gives قيس, Qays. The inspected 1905–1907 alternative edition reads قيس in the first genealogy as well. The extra yāʾ in the Arabic used here is retained; the difference does not by itself establish a second person.

Ibn Qāniʿ and Ibn Mandah transmitted through al-Ḥasan ibn Farqad, from al-Ḥasan, from Saʿd ibn Qays, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, who said: God said, ‘Son of Adam, pray four rakʿas at the beginning of the day, and I shall suffice you for its end.’ Ibn Mandah treated the subject of the first chain as a different man from the one from whom al-Ḥasan narrated, although he said of the first: His son ʿAbd Allāh and al-Ḥasan narrated from him.

records.arabic: بن مالك بن قريع بن ذهل بن الدئل بن مالك الأزدي أبو الكنود قال بن يونس وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعقد له راية على قومه سوداء فيها هلال أبيض وشهد فتح مصر وله بها عقب روى عنه ابنه القاسم بن أبي الكنود رواه سعيد بن عفير عن عمرو بن زهير بن أسمر بن أبي الكنود أن أبا الكنود وفد فذكره
records.english: ibn Mālik ibn Qurayʿ ibn Dhuhl ibn al-Duʾil ibn Mālik al-Azdī, Abū al-Kanūd. Ibn Yūnus said: He came as a delegate to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, who tied for him a black banner bearing a white crescent, to lead his people. He took part in the conquest of Egypt and had descendants there. His son al-Qāsim ibn Abī al-Kanūd narrated from him. Saʿīd ibn ʿUfayr transmitted the account from ʿAmr ibn Zuhayr ibn Asmar ibn Abī al-Kanūd: Abū al-Kanūd came as a delegate—and he related the account.

aliases: ʿAmr ibn Zuhayr ibn Asmar ibn Abī al-Kanūd

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: قال بن أبي حاتم عن أبيه قدم على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في وفد بني عذرة وروى الواقدي من طريق أبي عمرو بن حريث العبدري قال وجدت في كتاب آبائي قالوا قدم وفدنا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في صفر سنة تسع اثنا عشر رجلا منهم جمرة بن النعمان وسعد وسليم ابنا مالك
records.english: Ibn Abī Ḥātim said, on his father’s authority: He came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم with the delegation of Banū ʿUdhra. Al-Wāqidī transmitted through Abū ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth al-ʿAbdarī, who said: I found in the book of my forefathers that they said: Our delegation came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم in Ṣafar of the year 9, twelve men, among them Jamra ibn al-Nuʿmān, and Saʿd and Sulaym, the two sons of Mālik.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
ويقال له بن وهيب بن عبد مناف بن زهرة بن كلاب القرشي الزهري أبو إسحاق بن أبي وقاص أحد العشرة وآخرهم موتا وأمه حمنة بنت سفيان بن أمية بنت عم أبي سفيان بن حرب بن أمية روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كثيرا روى عنه بنوه إبراهيم وعامر ومصعب وعمر ومحمد وعائشة ومن الصحابة عائشة وابن عباس وابن عمر وجابر بن سمرة ومن كبار التابعين سعيد بن المسيب وأبو عثمان النهدي وقيس أي أبي حازم وعلقمة والأحنف وآخرون وكان أحد الفرسان وهو أول من رمى بسهم في سبيل الله وهو أحد الستة أهل الشورى وقال عمر إن أصابته الإمرة فذاك وإلا فليستعن به الوالي وكان رأس من فتح العراق وولي الكوفة لعمر وهو الذي بناها ثم عزل ووليها لعثمان وكان مجاب الدعوة مشهورا بذلك مات سنة إحدى وخمسين وقيل ست وقيل سبع وقيل ثمان والثاني أشهر وقد قيل إنه مات سنة خمس وقيل سنة أربع وقع في صحيح البخاري عنه أنه قال لقد مكثت سبعة أيام وإني لثالث الإسلام وقال إبراهيم بن المنذر كان هو وطلحة والزبير وعلى عذار عام واحد أي كان سنهم واحدا وروى الترمذي من حديث جابر قال أقبل سعد فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هذا خالي فليرني امرؤ خاله وقال بن إسحاق في المغازي كان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة يستخفون بصلاتهم فبينا سعد في شعب من شعاب مكة في نفر من الصحابة إذ ظهر عليهم المشركون فنافروهم وعابوا عليهم دينهم حتى قاتلوهم فضرب سعد رجلا من المشركين بلحى جمل فشجه فكان أول دم أريق في الإسلام وروى الترمذي من حديث قيس بن أبي حازم عن سعد أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال اللهم استجب لسعد إذا دعاك فكان لا يدعو إلا استجيب له وروينا في مجابي الدعوة لابن أبي الدنيا من طريق جرير عن مغيرة عن أبيه قال كانت امرأة قامتها قامة صبي فقالوا هذه ابنة سعد غمست يدها في طهورها فقال قطع الله يديك فما شبت بعد ولما قتل عثمان اعتزل الفتنة ولزم بيته وروى الشيخان والترمذي والنسائي من حديث عائشة قالت لما قدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة أرق فقال ليت رجلا صالحا من أصحابي يحرسني إذ سمعنا صوت السلاح فقال من هذا قال أنا سعد فقام وفي رواية ودعا له مات سعد بالعقيق وحمل إلى المدينة فصلي عليه في المسجد وقال الواقدي أثبت ما قيل في وقت وفاته أنها سنة خمس وخمسين وقال أبو نعيم مات سنة ثمان وخمسين قال الزبير هو الذي فتح مدائن كسرى وكان مستجاب الدعوة وهو الذي تولى الكوفة واعتزل الفتنة وجاءه بن أخيه هاشم بن عتبة فقال ههنا مائة ألف سيف يرونك أحق بهذا الأمر فقال أريد منها سيفا واحدا إذا ضربت به المؤمن لم يصنع شيئا وإذا ضربت به الكافر قطع وأخرج محمد بن عثمان بن أبي شيبة في تاريخه بسند جيد عن أبي إسحاق قال كان أشد أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أربعة عمر وعلي والزبير وسعد وروينا في مسند أبي يعلى من طريق شريك بن أبي نمر أخو بني عامر بن سعد بن أبي وقاص أن أباه حين رأى اختلاف أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وتفرقهم اشترى أرضا ميتة ثم خرج واعتزل فيها بأهله على ما قال وكان سعد من أحد الناس بصرا فرأى ذات يوم شيئا يزول فقال لمن معه ترون شيئا قالوا نرى شيئا كالطائر قال أرى راكبا على بعير ثم جاء بعد قليل عم سعد على بختى فقال سعد اللهم إنا نعوذ بك من شر ما جاء به وقال عمر في وصيته إن أصابت الإمرة سعدا فذاك وإلا فليستعن به الذي يلي الأمر فإني لم أعزله عن عجز ولا خيانة وكان عمر أمره على الكوفة سنة إحدى وعشرين ثم لما ولي عثمان أمره عليها ثم عزله بالوليد بن عقبة سنة خمس وعشرين وقال الزبير بن بكار حدثني بن أبي أويس عن جابر عن بكير بن مسمار عن عامر بن سعد عن أبيه قال كان رجل من المشركين قد أحرق المسلمين فنزعت له بسهم فأصيبت جبهته فوقع وانكشفت عورته فضحك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وسماه الواقدي في روايته حبان بن العرقة وزاد أنه رمى بسهم فأصاب ذيل أم أيمن وكانت جاءت تسقي الجرحى فضحك منها فدفع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لسعد سهما فوقع السهم في نحر حبان فوقع مستلقيا وبدت عورته فضحك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال استعاذ لها سعد وقال أبو العباس السراج في تاريخه حدثنا إسماعيل بن أبي الحارث حدثنا أبو النضر عن مبارك بن سعيد عن عبد بن بريدة عمن حدثه عن جرير أنه مر بعمر فسأله عن سعد بن أبي وقاص فقال تركته في ولايته أكرم الناس مقدرة وأقلهم قسوة هو لهم كالأم البرة يجمع لهم كما تجمع الذرة أشد الناس عن البأس وأحب قريش إلى الناس وقال الزبير حدثنا إبراهيم بن محمد بن عبد العزيز قال كان سعد في جيش عبيدة بن الحارث حين بعثه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى رابغ يلقى عير قريش فتراموا بالنبل وكان سعد أول من رمى بسهم في سبيل الله قال فحدثني محمد بن بجاد بن موسى عن سعد قال قال سعد في ذلك
ألا هل أتى رسول الله أني
حميت صحابتي بصدور نبلي قال وزاد فيها
أذود بها عدوهم ذيادا
بكل حزونة وبكل سهل
فما يعتد رام من معد
بسهم في سبيل الله قبلي وأخرجه يونس بن بكير في زياداته عن عثمان بن عبد الرحمن عن الزهري بنحوه وفيه الأبيات الثلاثة
records.english:
He is also called ibn Wuhayb. The lineage continues: ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Zuhra ibn Kilāb; al-Qurashī al-Zuhrī, Abū Isḥāq, Ibn Abī Waqqāṣ. He was one of the Ten and the last of them to die. His mother was Ḥamna bint Sufyān ibn Umayya, the paternal cousin of Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb ibn Umayya. He narrated many reports from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. His children Ibrāhīm, ʿĀmir, Muṣʿab, ʿUmar, Muḥammad, and ʿĀʾisha narrated from him. Among the Companions, ʿĀʾisha, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, and Jābir ibn Samura narrated from him; among the senior Successors, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, Qays [ibn] Abī Ḥāzim, ʿAlqama, al-Aḥnaf, and others.

Editorial note: The transmitter list reads قيس أي أبي حازم. The bracketed ibn is supplied from the inspected 1905–1907 alternative edition, which reads قيس بن أبي حازم. The same name also appears intact later in this account. The Arabic wording is unchanged.

He was one of the horsemen and the first to shoot an arrow in God's cause. He was also one of the six members of the consultative council. ʿUmar said: ‘If the command falls to him, so be it; otherwise, let the governor seek his assistance.’ He led those who conquered Iraq and governed Kufa for ʿUmar; it was he who founded it. He was then dismissed, and later governed it for ʿUthmān. He was renowned for having his prayers answered. He died in the year 51; it is also said 56, 57, or 58, the second being the more widely known account. It has also been said that he died in 55, or in 54.

In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī he is reported to have said: ‘For seven days I remained the third person in Islam.’ Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir said: ‘He, Ṭalḥa, al-Zubayr, and ʿAlī reached the age of first beard-growth in the same year’—that is, they were the same age. Al-Tirmidhī transmitted a report from Jābir, who said: Saʿd approached, and the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said: ‘This is my maternal uncle; let a man show me his maternal uncle!’

Ibn Isḥāq said in al-Maghāzī: The Companions of God's Messenger صلى الله عليه وسلم used to conceal their prayers in Mecca. While Saʿd was in one of Mecca's ravines with a group of the Companions, the polytheists came upon them. They quarrelled with them and disparaged their religion, until they fought them. Saʿd struck one of the polytheists with a camel's jawbone and cut his head. This was the first blood shed in Islam.

Al-Tirmidhī transmitted, from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, from Saʿd, that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said: ‘O God, answer Saʿd when he calls upon You.’ Thereafter he never prayed without being answered. We have transmitted in Ibn Abī al-Dunyā's Mujābī al-Daʿwa, through Jarīr, from Mughīra, from his father, who said: There was a woman whose height was that of a child. They said: This is Saʿd's daughter. She dipped her hand into her ablution water, and he said: ‘May God cut off your two hands!’ She did not grow after that.

When ʿUthmān was killed, he withdrew from the civil strife and kept to his home. The two shaykhs, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Nasāʾī transmitted a report from ʿĀʾisha, who said: When the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم arrived in Medina, he lay awake and said: ‘Would that a righteous man among my Companions would guard me.’ Just then we heard the sound of weapons. He asked: ‘Who is this?’ He replied: ‘I am Saʿd.’ He stood up; another version says: ‘And he prayed for him.’

Saʿd died at al-ʿAqīq and was carried to Medina, where the funeral prayer over him was performed in the mosque. Al-Wāqidī said: The best-established statement about the time of his death places it in the year 55. Abū Nuʿaym said: He died in the year 58. Al-Zubayr said: He was the one who conquered the cities of Kisrā. His prayers were answered; he was the one who governed Kufa and withdrew from the civil strife. His nephew Hāshim ibn ʿUtba came to him and said: ‘Here are a hundred thousand swords whose bearers consider you most entitled to this command.’ He replied: ‘I want a single sword among them which does nothing when I strike a believer with it, but cuts when I strike an unbeliever with it.’

Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shayba recorded in his History, with a good chain, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: The four strongest Companions of God's Messenger صلى الله عليه وسلم were ʿUmar, ʿAlī, al-Zubayr, and Saʿd.

We have transmitted in Abū Yaʿlā's Musnad, through Sharīk ibn Abī Nimr—‘brother of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ’—that his father, when he saw the disagreement and division among the Companions of God's Messenger صلى الله عليه وسلم, bought uncultivated land, then went out and withdrew there with his family, as he put it. Saʿd was among the keenest-sighted of people. One day he saw something moving and said to those with him: ‘Do you see anything?’ They replied: ‘We see something like a bird.’ He said: ‘I see a rider on a camel.’ A little later, Saʿd's paternal uncle arrived on a Bactrian camel. Saʿd said: ‘O God, we seek refuge in You from the evil of what he has brought.’

Editorial note: The words أخو بني عامر بن سعد بن أبي وقاص أن أباه leave the connection after Sharīk and the antecedent of “his father” unclear. The inspected 1905–1907 alternative edition repeats this wording. No missing narrator or definite paternal referent has been supplied.

ʿUmar said in his final directions: ‘If the command falls to Saʿd, so be it; otherwise, let whoever assumes command seek his assistance, for I did not dismiss him for incapacity or dishonesty.’ ʿUmar had appointed him over Kufa in the year 21. When ʿUthmān assumed office, he appointed him over it, then replaced him with al-Walīd ibn ʿUqba in the year 25.

Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār said: Ibn Abī Uways related to me, from Jābir, from Bukayr ibn Mismār, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from his father, who said: A man among the polytheists had grievously harmed the Muslims. I drew my bow at him with an arrow, and his forehead was struck. He fell, and his private parts were exposed, whereupon God's Messenger صلى الله عليه وسلم laughed. In his version, al-Wāqidī named him Ḥibbān ibn al-ʿAriqa. He added that the man shot an arrow which struck the hem of Umm Ayman's garment. She had come to give the wounded water, and he laughed at her. God's Messenger صلى الله عليه وسلم handed Saʿd an arrow. The arrow struck Ḥibbān in the throat; he fell on his back, and his private parts were exposed. God's Messenger صلى الله عليه وسلم laughed and said: ‘Saʿd sought protection for her.’

Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Sarrāj said in his History: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī al-Ḥārith related to us; Abū al-Naḍr related to us, from Mubārak ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAbd ibn Burayda, from someone who related to him, from Jarīr, that he passed by ʿUmar, who asked him about Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ. He said: ‘I left him in his governorship, the most generous of men in the exercise of power and the least harsh. He is like a devoted mother to them, gathering for them as the tiny ant gathers; the strongest of men [in battle], and the most beloved man of Quraysh among the people.’

Editorial note: “In battle” is a supplied reading. The Arabic used here has عن البأس; the inspected 1905–1907 alternative edition reads عند البأس, supporting a statement about strength in battle. The Arabic source wording is retained.

Al-Zubayr said: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us: Saʿd was in the force of ʿUbayda ibn al-Ḥārith when God's Messenger صلى الله عليه وسلم sent him to Rābigh to meet the caravan of Quraysh. They exchanged arrows, and Saʿd was the first to shoot an arrow in God's cause. He said: Muḥammad ibn Bijād ibn Mūsā related to me, from Saʿd, who said: Saʿd said concerning this:

Has word reached God's Messenger that I
protected my companions with the points of my arrows?

He said: He added to it:

With them I drive their enemy away,
over every rugged height and every level plain.
No archer of Maʿadd can count an arrow
in God's cause before mine.

Yūnus ibn Bukayr recorded a similar account in his Additions, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from al-Zuhrī; it contains the three verses.

records.arabic: بن ثعلبة بن حارثة بن عمرو بن الخزرج بن ساعدة الأنصاري الساعدي والد سهل بن سعد قال الواقدي حدثنا أبي بن عباس بن سهل عن أبيه عن جده قال تجهز سعد بن مالك ليخرج إلى بدر فمرض فمات فضرب له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بسهمه وأجره وأخرجه الحارث في مسنده عن يعقوب بن محمد الزهري عن عبد المهيمن بن العباس بن سهل عن أبيه وزاد فيه فكتب وصيته في آخر رحله وأوصى للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم برحله وراحلته وأخرج أبو نعيم من وجه آخر عن أبي بن عباس عن أبيه عن جده قال كان للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عند أبي أفراس الحديث وسمى أبو نعيم أباه سعدا والمعروف أن اسمه مالك
records.english:
ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥārithah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Khazraj ibn Sāʿida al-Anṣārī al-Sāʿidī, the father of Sahl ibn Saʿd. Al-Wāqidī said: Ubayy ibn ʿAbbās ibn Sahl related to us, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: Saʿd ibn Mālik prepared to set out for Badr, but fell ill and died. God's Messenger صلى الله عليه وسلم allotted him his share and reward. Al-Ḥārith recorded it in his Musnad, from Yaʿqūb ibn Muḥammad al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Muhaymin ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn Sahl, from his father, adding: He wrote his will on the rear of his saddle and bequeathed his saddle and riding camel to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم.

Abū Nuʿaym recorded by another route, from Ubayy ibn ʿAbbās, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: ‘The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم had horses with my father’—the report. Abū Nuʿaym named his father Saʿd, whereas his well-known name is Mālik.

records.arabic: بن عبيد بن ثعلبة بن الأبجر وهو خدرة بن عوف بن الحارث بن الخزرج الأنصاري الخزرجي أبو سعيد الخدري مشهور بكنيته استصغر بأحد واستشهد أبوه بها وغزا هو ما بعدها روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الكثير وروى عن أبي بكر وعمر وعثمان وعلي وزيد بن ثابت وغيرهم روى عنه من الصحابة بن عباس وابن عمر وجابر ومحمود بن لبيد وأبو أمامة بن سهل وأبو الطفيل ومن كبار التابعين بن المسيب وأبو عثمان النهدي وطارق بن شهاب وعبيد بن عمير وممن بعدهم عطاء وعياض بن عبد الله بن أبي سرح وبشر بن سعيد ومجاهد وأبو المتوكل الناجي وأبو نضرة ومعبد بن سيرين وعبد الله بن محيريز وآخرون وهو مكثر من الحديث قال حنظلة بن أبي سفيان عن أشياخه كان من أفقه أحداث الصحابة وقال الخطيب كان من أفاضل الصحابة وحفظ حديثا كثيرا وروى الهيثم بن كليب في مسنده من طريق عبد المهيمن بن عباس بن سهل بن سعد عن أبيه عن جده قال بايعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنا وأبو ذر وعبادة بن الصامت ومحمد بن مسلمة وأبو سعيد الخدري وسادس على ألا تأخذنا في الله لومة لائم فاستقال السادس فأقاله وروى ابن سعد من طريق حنظلة بن سفيان الجمحي عن أشياخه قال لم يكن أحد من أحداث أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أفقه من أبي سعيد الخدري ومن طريق يزيد بن عبد الله بن الشخير قال خرج أبو سعيد يوم الحرة فدخل غارا فدخل عليه شامي فقال اخرج فقال لا أخرج وإن تدخل علي أقتلك فدخل عليه فوضع أبو سعيد السيف وقال بؤ بإثمك قال أنت أبو سعيد الخدري قال نعم قال فاستغفر لي وروى أحمد وغيره من طريق عطية عن أبي سعيد قال قتل أبي يوم أحد شهيدا وتركنا بغير مال فأتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أسأله فحين رآني قال من استغنى أغناه الله ومن يستعف يعفه الله فرجعت وأصل هذا الحديث في الصحيحين من طريق عطاء بن يزيد عن أبي سعيد بقصة أخرى غير هذه ولفظه من يستغن يغنه الله ومن يستعفف يعفه الله ومن يتصبر يصبره الله الحديث قال شعبة عن أبي سلمة سمعت أبا نضرة عن أبي سعيد رفعه لا يمنعن أحدكم مخافة الناس أن يتكلم بالحق إذا رآه أو علمه وقال أبو سعيد فحملني ذلك على أن ركبت إلى معاوية فملأت أذنيه ثم رجعت وقال بن خيثمة حدثنا يحيى بن معين حدثنا عمرو بن محمد بن عمرو بن معاذ الأنصاري سمعت هند ابنة سعيد بن أبي سعيد الخدري عن عمها جاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عائدا إلى أبي سعيد فقدمنا إليه ذراع شاة وقال سعيد بن منصور حدثنا خلف بن خليفة عن العلاء بن المسيب عن أبيه عن أبي سعيد قلنا له هنيئا لك برؤية رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وصحبته قال إنك لا تدري ما أحدثنا بعده وقال علي بن الجعد حدثنا شعبة عن سعيد بن يزيد سمع أبا نضرة يحدث عن أبي سعيد قال تحدثوا فإن الحديث يهيج الحديث قال الواقدي مات سنة أربع وسبعين وقيل أربع وستين وقال المدائني مات سنة ثلاث وستين وقال العسكري مات سنة خمس وستين
records.english:
ibn ʿUbayd ibn Thaʿlabah ibn al-Abjar, who is Khudra, ibn ʿAwf ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī. He is well known by his kunya. He was deemed too young at Uḥud; his father was martyred there, and he himself took part in the campaigns that followed. He narrated many reports from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, and also narrated from Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Zayd ibn Thābit, and others. Among the Companions, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, Jābir, Maḥmūd ibn Labīd, Abū Umāma ibn Sahl, and Abū al-Ṭufayl narrated from him. Among the senior Successors were Ibn al-Musayyab, Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb, and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr; among those after them were ʿAṭāʾ, ʿIyāḍ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Sarḥ, Bishr ibn Saʿīd, Mujāhid, Abū al-Mutawakkil al-Nājī, Abū Naḍra, Maʿbad ibn Sīrīn, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥayrīz, and others. He was a prolific transmitter of hadith.

Ḥanẓala ibn Abī Sufyān said, from his elders: He was among the most knowledgeable in religious law of the younger Companions. Al-Khaṭīb said: He was one of the eminent Companions and preserved a great many reports. Al-Haytham ibn Kulayb transmitted in his Musnad, through ʿAbd al-Muhaymin ibn ʿAbbās ibn Sahl ibn Saʿd, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I, Abū Dharr, ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit, Muḥammad ibn Maslama, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, and a sixth man pledged allegiance to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, undertaking that no reproach from anyone would deter us in God's cause. The sixth man asked to be released, and he released him.

Ibn Saʿd transmitted through Ḥanẓala ibn Sufyān al-Jumaḥī, from his elders, who said: None of the younger Companions of God's Messenger صلى الله عليه وسلم was more knowledgeable in religious law than Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī. Through Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, who said: Abū Saʿīd went out on the day of al-Ḥarra and entered a cave. A Syrian came upon him and said: ‘Come out.’ He replied: ‘I will not come out; if you come in upon me, I will kill you.’ The man came in upon him, but Abū Saʿīd laid down his sword and said: ‘Bear your sin.’ He asked: ‘Are you Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī?’ He replied: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Then ask forgiveness for me.’

Aḥmad and others transmitted through ʿAṭiyya, from Abū Saʿīd, who said: My father was killed as a martyr on the day of Uḥud and left us without any wealth. I came to God's Messenger صلى الله عليه وسلم to ask him for help. When he saw me, he said: ‘Whoever seeks to be self-sufficient, God will make him self-sufficient; whoever seeks to refrain from asking, God will help him refrain.’ So I went back. The basis of this report is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, through ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd, from Abū Saʿīd, with a story other than this one. Its wording is: ‘Whoever seeks self-sufficiency, God will make him self-sufficient; whoever seeks to refrain from asking, God will help him refrain; and whoever seeks to be patient, God will grant him patience’—the report.

Shuʿba said, from Abū Salama: I heard Abū Naḍra relate from Abū Saʿīd, attributing it to the Prophet: ‘Let fear of people never prevent any of you from speaking the truth when he sees or knows it.’ Abū Saʿīd said: This prompted me to ride to Muʿāwiya and fill his ears, then return.

Ibn Khaythama said: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn related to us; ʿAmr ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Muʿādh al-Anṣārī related to us: I heard Hind, the daughter of Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Khudrī, relate from her paternal uncle: God's Messenger صلى الله عليه وسلم came to visit Abū Saʿīd when he was ill, and we served him a sheep's foreleg.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr said: Khalaf ibn Khalīfa related to us, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Musayyab, from his father, from Abū Saʿīd: We said to him, ‘How fortunate you are to have seen God's Messenger صلى الله عليه وسلم and enjoyed his company!’ He said: ‘You do not know what we introduced after him.’

ʿAlī ibn al-Jaʿd said: Shuʿba related to us, from Saʿīd ibn Yazīd, who heard Abū Naḍra relate from Abū Saʿīd, who said: ‘Relate reports to one another, for one report brings another to mind.’ Al-Wāqidī said: He died in the year 74; it is also said 64. Al-Madāʾinī said: He died in the year 63. Al-ʿAskarī said: He died in the year 65.

records.arabic: بن مسعود بن كعب الأنصاري الأوسي يأتي نسبه في ترجمة أبيه قال البغوي ذكره محمد بن إسماعيل في الصحابة ولم أجد له حديثا وروى عبد الرزاق عن معمر عن الزهري عن حرام بن سعد بن محيصة عن أبيه أن ناقة للبراء بن عازب دخلت حائط قوم فأفسدت فقضى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن حفظ الأموال على أهلها بالنهار الحديث اختلف فيه على الزهري اختلاف كثيرا وقال الذهلي وأبو داود في التفرد لم يتابع عبد الرزاق على قوله عن أبيه وقد رواه مالك وإلياس عن الزهري عن حرام بن سعد مرسلا وقال بن عبد البر في التمهيد ليست له صحبة وإنما روايته عن أبيه وروى بن أبي شيبة عن بن عيينة عن الزهري عن حرام بن سعد عن أبيه أن محيصة سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن كسب الحجام الحديث وقال الذهلي رواه مالك وغيره عن الزهري عن أبن محيصة عن أبيه وقول من قال عن حرام عن أبيه هو المحفوظ
records.english:
ibn Masʿūd ibn Kaʿb, al-Anṣārī al-Awsī. His lineage will appear in his father's biography. Al-Baghawī said: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl listed him among the Companions, but I have found no report from him. ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ḥarām ibn Saʿd ibn Muḥayyiṣah, from his father, that a she-camel belonging to al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib entered some people's walled garden and damaged it. God's Messenger صلى الله عليه وسلم ruled that owners were responsible for guarding their property by day—the report. The versions transmitted from al-Zuhrī differ greatly. Al-Dhuhlī and Abū Dāwūd, in al-Tafarrud, said: No one corroborated ʿAbd al-Razzāq's wording ‘from his father.’ Mālik and Ilyās transmitted it from al-Zuhrī, from Ḥarām ibn Saʿd, as a mursal report, with the intervening narrator omitted. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said in al-Tamhīd: He was not a Companion; rather, he narrated from his father.

Ibn Abī Shayba transmitted from Ibn ʿUyayna, from al-Zuhrī, from Ḥarām ibn Saʿd, from his father, that Muḥayyiṣah asked the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم about a cupper's earnings—the report. Al-Dhuhlī said: Mālik and others transmitted it from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn Muḥayyiṣah, from his father. The wording of those who said ‘from Ḥarām, from his father’ is the correctly preserved version.

records.arabic: ويقال بالمثناة بدل الدال ذكره بن حبان في الصحابة وقال من أهل الشام وقال بن منده يعد في أهل حمص وروى بن السكن والباوردي من طريق محفوظ بن علقمة عن عبد الرحمن بن عائد سمعت سعد بن المدحاس يقول سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول من كذب علي الحديث وروى بن حبان من هذا الوجه عنه قال غزونا مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وروى الطبراني في مسند الشاميين من هذا الوجه قال بن عائد قال أبو أمامة قال سعد بن المدحاس وكان من الصحابة قال أريت في المنام إني وردت عينا فإذا الناس من جاء منهم بسقاء ملأه صغيرا كان أو كبيرا فقلت ما هذا قيل القرآن فحلف سعد حينئذ ليقرأن البقرة وآل عمران
records.english:
also given with the two-dotted letter in place of dāl. Ibn Ḥibbān listed him among the Companions and said: He was one of the people of Syria. Ibn Manda said: He is counted among the people of Homs. Ibn al-Sakan and al-Bāwardī transmitted through Maḥfūẓ ibn ʿAlqama, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀʾid: I heard Saʿd ibn al-Midḥās say: I heard God's Messenger صلى الله عليه وسلم say, ‘Whoever lies about me’—the report. Ibn Ḥibbān transmitted by this route from him, who said: ‘We went on campaign with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم.’

Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted by this route in Musnad al-Shāmiyyīn: Ibn ʿĀʾid said: Abū Umāma said: Saʿd ibn al-Midḥās, who was one of the Companions, said: I was shown in a dream that I came to a spring. Whenever someone brought a waterskin, he filled it, whether it was small or large. I asked: ‘What is this?’ I was told: ‘The Qurʾān.’ Saʿd then swore that he would recite al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān.
