records.arabic: بن سعيد بن العاص بن أمية القرشي الأموي أبو عثمان بن أخي سعيد بن سعيد الماضي قريبا أمه أم كلثوم بنت عبد الله بن أبي قيس بن عمرو العامرية ولم يكن للعاص ولد غير سعيد المذكور قال بن أبي حاتم عن أبيه له صحبة قلت كان له يوم مات النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تسع سنين وقتل أبوه يوم بدر قتله علي ويقال إن عمر قال لسعيد بن العاص لم أقتل أباك وإنما قتلت خالي العاص بن هشام فقال ولو قتلته لكنت على الحق وكان على الباطل فأعجبه قوله وكان من فصحاء قريش ولهذا ندبه عثمان فيمن ندب لكتابة القرآن قال بن أبي داود في المصاحف حدثنا العباس بن الوليد حدثنا أبي حدثنا سعيد بن عبد العزيز أن عربية القرآن أقيمت على لسان سعيد بن العاص لأنه كان أشبههم لهجة برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وولي الكوفة وغزا طبرستان ففتحها وغزا جرجان وكان في عسكره حذيفة وغيره من كبار الصحابة وولي المدينة لمعاوية وله حديث في الترمذي من رواية أيوب بن موسى بن عمرو بن سعيد بن العاص عن أبيه عن جده إن كان الضمير يعود على موسى وله آخر في ترجمة جده يأتي في القسم الأخير وروى الزبير من طريق عبد العزيز بن أبان عن خالد بن سعيد عن أبيه عن بن عمر قال جاءت امرأة إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ببردة فقالت إني نذرت أن أعطي هذه البردة لأكرم العرب فقال أعطيها لهذا الغلام وهو واقف يعني سعيدا هذا قال الزبير والثياب السعدية تنسب إليه وروى له مسلم والنسائي من روايته عن عثمان وعائشة وروى الهيثم بن كليب في مسنده من طريق سعيد بن عمرو بن سعيد بن العاص عن أبيه عن جده سمعت عمر يقول فذكر له حديثا وسيأتي له ذكر في ترجمة جده في القسم الأخير وأخرج الطبراني من طريق محمد بن قانع بن جبير بن مطعم عن أبيه عن جده قال رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عاد سعيد بن العاص فرأيته يكمده بخرقة وسعيد بن العاص هذا يحتمل أن يكون صاحب الترجمة وتكون رواية جبير هذه بعد الفتح ويحتمل أن يكون جده وتكون رؤية جبير له قبل الهجرة ولا مانع من عيادة الكافر ولا سيما في ذلك الزمان لم يكن أذن فيه في قتال الكفار وذكر بن سعد في ترجمته قصة ولايته على الكوفة بعد الوليد بن عقبة لعثمان وشكوى أهل الكوفة منه وعزله مطولا وكان معاوية عاتبه على تخلفه عنه في حروبه فاعتذر ثم ولاه المدينة فكان يعاقب بينه وبين مروان في ولايتها وروى بن أبي خيثمة من طريق يحيى بن سعيد قال قدم محمد بن عقيل بن أبي طالب على أبيه فقال له من أشرف الناس قال أنا وابن أمي وحسبك بسعيد بن العاص وقال معاوية كريمة قريش سعيد بن العاص وكان مشهورا بالكرم والبر حتى كان إذا سأله السائل وليس عنده ما يعطيه كتب له بما يريد أن يعطيه مسطورا فلما مات كان عليه ثمانون ألف دينار فوفاها عنه ولده عمرو الأشدق وحج سعيد بالناس في سنة تسع وأربعين أو سنة اثنتين وخمسين ولبث بعدها ذكر ذلك يعقوب بن سفيان في تاريخه عن يحيى بن كثير عن الليث وروى عن صالح بن كيسان قال كان سعيد بن العاص حليما وقورا وكان إذا أحب شيئا أو أبغضه لم يذكر ذلك ويقول إن القلوب تتغير فلا ينبغي للمرء أن يكون مادحا اليوم عائبا غدا ومن محاسن كلامه لا تمازح الشريف فيحقد عليك ولا تمازح الدنيء فتهون عليه ذكره في المجالسة من طريق أبي عبيدة وأخرجه بن أبي الدنيا من وجه آخر عن بن المبارك ومن كلامه موطنان لا أعتذر من العي فيهما إذا خاطبت جاهلا أو طلبت حاجة لنفسي ذكره في المجالسة من طريق الأصمعي وقال مصعب الزبيري كان يقال له عكة العسل وقال الزبير بن بكار مات سعيد في قصره بالعقيق سنة ثلاث وخمسين
records.english:
ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ ibn Umayyah, al-Qurashī al-Umawī, Abū ʿUthmān, the nephew of Saʿīd ibn Saʿīd, who appeared shortly before. His mother was Umm Kulthūm bint ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qays ibn ʿAmr al-ʿĀmiriyyah. Al-ʿĀṣ had no child other than this Saʿīd. Ibn Abī Ḥātim reported from his father that he had companionship.

I say: He was nine years old when the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم died. His father was killed at Badr, killed by ʿAlī. It is said that ʿUmar told Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ, “I did not kill your father. I killed my maternal uncle, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Hishām.” He replied, “Even if you had killed him, you would have been in the right and he in the wrong.” His reply pleased ʿUmar.

He was one of Quraysh’s eloquent speakers, which is why ʿUthmān chose him among those assigned to write the Qurʾan. Ibn Abī Dāwūd said in al-Maṣāḥif: “Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd related to us; my father related to us; Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us that the Arabic of the Qurʾan was established according to the speech of Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ, because his manner of speech was the closest among them to that of the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم.”

He governed Kufa, campaigned in Ṭabaristān and conquered it, and campaigned in Jurjān. His army included Ḥudhayfah and other leading Companions. He governed Medina for Muʿāwiyah. He has a report in al-Tirmidhī through the narration of Ayyūb ibn Mūsā ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ, from his father, from his grandfather—if the pronoun refers to Mūsā. He has another report in his grandfather’s biography, which will appear in the final section.

Al-Zubayr transmitted through ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abān, from Khālid ibn Saʿīd, from his father, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: “A woman came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم with a cloak and said, ‘I vowed to give this cloak to the noblest of the Arabs.’ He said, ‘Give it to this boy,’ who was standing there”—meaning this Saʿīd. Al-Zubayr said that the Saʿdī garments are named after him.

Muslim and al-Nasāʾī transmitted his narrations from ʿUthmān and ʿĀʾishah. Al-Haytham ibn Kulayb transmitted in his Musnad through Saʿīd ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ, from his father, from his grandfather: “I heard ʿUmar say...” He cited a report from him. Saʿīd will also be mentioned in his grandfather’s biography in the final section.

Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted through Muḥammad ibn Qāniʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: “I saw the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم visit Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ during his illness, and I saw him applying a warm compress to him with a cloth.” This Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ may be the subject of the present biography, in which case Jubayr’s account would concern a time after the conquest. He may instead be his grandfather, in which case Jubayr would have seen him before the emigration. There is nothing to preclude visiting an unbeliever when he is ill, particularly at that time, when permission to fight the unbelievers had not yet been given.

In his biography, Ibn Saʿd related at length the story of Saʿīd’s appointment as governor of Kufa for ʿUthmān after al-Walīd ibn ʿUqbah, the Kufans’ complaints against him, and his dismissal. Muʿāwiyah reproached him for failing to join him in his wars, and he offered an excuse. Muʿāwiyah then appointed him governor of Medina, alternating its governorship between him and Marwān.

Ibn Abī Khaythamah transmitted through Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, who said: “Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib came to his father and asked him, ‘Who are the noblest people?’ He replied, ‘I and the son of my mother; and Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ is example enough for you.’” Muʿāwiyah said, “The noblest of Quraysh is Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ.” He was renowned for generosity and kindness, so much so that when a petitioner asked him for something and he had nothing to give, he wrote him a document specifying what he wished to give him. When he died, he owed eighty thousand dinars. His son ʿAmr al-Ashdaq paid them on his behalf.

Saʿīd led the people on pilgrimage in the year forty-nine or fifty-two, and lived on after that. Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān mentioned this in his History, from Yaḥyā ibn Kathīr, from al-Layth. He also transmitted from Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, who said: “Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ was forbearing and dignified. When he liked or disliked something, he did not mention it. He would say, ‘Hearts change, so a person should not praise something today and find fault with it tomorrow.’”

Among his fine sayings was: “Do not joke with a man of high standing, lest he bear a grudge against you; and do not joke with a base man, lest he hold you in contempt.” This was mentioned in al-Mujālasah through Abū ʿUbaydah. Ibn Abī al-Dunyā transmitted it by another route from Ibn al-Mubārak. Another of his sayings was: “There are two situations in which I make no apology for being inarticulate: when I address an ignorant person, or ask for something for myself.” It was mentioned in al-Mujālasah through al-Aṣmaʿī. Muṣʿab al-Zubayrī said that he used to be called “the honey-skin.” Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār said that Saʿīd died in his palace at al-ʿAqīq in the year fifty-three.

records.arabic: بن المغيرة بن عبد الله بن عمر بن مخزوم المخزومي له حديث ذكر نسبه الذهبي في التجريد فقال ما نصه سعيد بن العاص بن هشام بن المغيرة المخزومي جد عكرمة بن خالد إن صح ففي معجم الطبراني حدثنا مطين حدثنا سفيان حدثنا حماد بن سلمة عن عكرمة بن خالد عن أبيه عن جده قال إذا وقع الطاعون لكن سها هنا الطبراني فأورده في الخاء يعني في خالد بن العاص قلت هذا الحديث قد ذكرته وبينت شاهد ذلك وتحريره في القسم الرابع في ترجمة العاص بن هشام في حرف العين كما سيأتي إن شاء الله تعالى فإن الذهبي ترجم للعاص بن هشام هناك تبعا للطبراني وأبي نعيم وأبي موسى
records.english:
ibn al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Makhzūm, al-Makhzūmī. He has a report. Al-Dhahabī gave his lineage in al-Tajrīd, saying in these words: “Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ ibn Hishām ibn al-Mughīrah al-Makhzūmī, the grandfather of ʿIkrimah ibn Khālid, if this is sound. In al-Ṭabarānī’s Muʿjam: ‘Muṭayyan related to us; Sufyān related to us; Ḥammād ibn Salamah related to us, from ʿIkrimah ibn Khālid, from his father, from his grandfather, who said, “When the plague breaks out...”’ But al-Ṭabarānī made an oversight here and placed it under khāʾ”—meaning under Khālid ibn al-ʿĀṣ.

I say: I have mentioned this report, set out the corroborating evidence, and clarified it in the fourth section, in the biography of al-ʿĀṣ ibn Hishām under the letter ʿayn, as will appear إن شاء الله تعالى. Al-Dhahabī entered al-ʿĀṣ ibn Hishām there, following al-Ṭabarānī, Abū Nuʿaym, and Abū Mūsā.

records.arabic: بن سلامان بن ربيعة بن سعد بن جمح القرشي الجمحي من كبار الصحابة وفضلائهم وأمه أروى بنت أبي معيط أسلم قبل خيبر وهاجر فشهدها وما بعدها وولاه عمر حمص وكان مشهورا بالخير والزهد وروى عنه عبد الرحمن بن سابط الجمحي وأرسل عنه شهر بن حوشب وغيره وروى أبو يعلى من رواية بن سابط عن سعيد بن حذيم قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لو أن امرأة من الحور العين أخرجت يدها لوجد ريحها كل ذي روح الحديث مختصرا أخرجه أبو أحمد الحاكم وابن سعد مطولا وفيه قصة لسعيد مع زوجته في تفرقته المال الذي يأتيه من عطائه وروى محمد بن عثمان بن أبي شيبة في تاريخه من طريق زيد بن أسلم قال قال عمر لسعيد بن عامر بن حذيم إن أهل الشام يحبونك قال لأني أعاونهم وأواسيهم فقال خذ هذه عشرة آلاف فتوسع بها قال أعطها من هو أحوج إليها مني الحديث وروى بن سعد من طريق بن سابط قال أرسل عمر إلى سعيد بن عامر إني مستعملك فقال لا تعنتني قال إنما أبعثك على قوم لست بأفضلهم ولست أبعثك لتضرب أبشارهم ولا لتهتك أعراضهم ولكن تجاهد بهم عدوهم وتقسم بينهم فيأهم وروى أبو يعلى والحسن بن سفيان والبغوي من طريق بن سابط أيضا عن سعيد بن عامر سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول يجيء فقراء المسلمين يزفون فيقال لهم قفوا في الحساب فيقولون والله ما كان لنا شيء نحاسب عليه فيقول الله صدق عبادي فيدخلون الجنة قبل الناس بسبعين عاما قال بن سعد في الطبقة الثالثة مات سنة عشرين وهو وال على بعض الشام لعمر وروى البخاري من طريق الزهري قال مات في زمن عمر وقال أبو بكر البغدادي في تسمية من نزل حمص من الصحابة استعمله عمر على حمص بعد عياض فوليها دون نصف سنة ومات ولي في المحرم سنة عشرين ومات في جمادى الأولى وأرخه الهيثم بن عدي وابن زبر سنة تسع عشرة زاد الهيثم ومات بقيسارية وقال أبو عبيد مات سنة إحدى وعشرين فالله أعلم
records.english:
ibn Salāmān ibn Rabīʿah ibn Saʿd ibn Jumaḥ, al-Qurashī al-Jumaḥī, one of the leading and distinguished Companions. His mother was Arwā bint Abī Muʿayṭ. He embraced Islam before Khaybar and emigrated, taking part in that campaign and those after it. ʿUmar appointed him governor of Homs. He was renowned for goodness and asceticism. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sābiṭ al-Jumaḥī narrated from him, while Shahr ibn Ḥawshab and others transmitted from him without a continuous chain.

Abū Yaʿlā transmitted through Ibn Sābiṭ, from Saʿīd ibn Ḥudhaym, who said: “The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said, ‘If a woman from the wide-eyed maidens of Paradise extended her hand, every living being would smell her fragrance.’” This is an abridgment of the report. Abū Aḥmad al-Ḥākim and Ibn Saʿd transmitted it at length. It includes a story about Saʿīd and his wife concerning his giving away the money he received as his stipend.

Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah transmitted in his History through Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: “ʿUmar said to Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir ibn Ḥudhaym, ‘The people of Syria love you.’ He replied, ‘Because I help them and share with them.’ He said, ‘Take these ten thousand and use them to make your circumstances easier.’ He replied, ‘Give them to someone who needs them more than I do.’” The report continues.

Ibn Saʿd transmitted through Ibn Sābiṭ, who said: “ʿUmar sent word to Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir: ‘I am appointing you to office.’ He replied, ‘Do not put me to hardship.’ He said, ‘I am only sending you over people whom you are no better than. I am not sending you to flog their bodies or violate their honor, but to fight their enemy with them and distribute their revenues, the fayʾ, among them.’”

Abū Yaʿlā, al-Ḥasan ibn Sufyān, and al-Baghawī also transmitted through Ibn Sābiṭ, from Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir: “I heard the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم say, ‘The poor Muslims will come hastening along. They will be told, “Stop for the reckoning.” They will say, “By God, we had nothing for which to be called to account.” God will say, “My servants have spoken the truth.” They will enter Paradise seventy years before the other people.’”

Ibn Saʿd said in the third class that he died in the year twenty while governing part of Syria for ʿUmar. Al-Bukhārī transmitted through al-Zuhrī that he died during ʿUmar’s time. Abū Bakr al-Baghdādī said in his list of the Companions who settled in Homs: “ʿUmar appointed him over Homs after ʿIyāḍ. He governed it for less than half a year and died. He was appointed in Muḥarram of the year twenty and died in Jumādā al-Ūlā.” Al-Haytham ibn ʿAdī and Ibn Zabr dated his death to the year nineteen. Al-Haytham added that he died at Caesarea. Abū ʿUbayd said that he died in the year twenty-one. فالله أعلم.

records.arabic: وقيل سعيد بن عبيد بن قيس بن لقيط بن عامر بن أمية أو ربيعة بن ظرب بن الحارث بن فهر القرشي الفهري ذكر بن شاهين من طريق بن الكلبي وغيره أنه أسلم قديما وهاجر إلى الحبشة وذكر البلاذري أنه قدم المدينة قبل جعفر بن أبي طالب وهو أخو نافع بن عبد قيس
records.english: also given as Saʿīd ibn ʿUbayd ibn Qays ibn Laqīṭ ibn ʿĀmir ibn Umayya or Rabīʿa ibn Ẓarib ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Fihr, al-Qurashī al-Fihrī. Ibn Shāhīn mentioned, through Ibn al-Kalbī and others, that he embraced Islam early and emigrated to Abyssinia. Al-Balādhurī mentioned that he arrived in Medina before Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib. He was the brother of Nāfiʿ ibn ʿAbd Qays.

records.arabic: بن علاج بن أبي سلمة بن عبد العزى بن غيرة بن عوف بن ثقيف الثقفي جد إسماعيل بن طريح الشاعر روى بن منده من طريق إسماعيل حدثني أبي عن جدي أن أبا سفيان رمى سعيد بن عبيد جده يوم الطائف بسهم فأصاب عينه فأتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا رسول الله إن هذه عيني أصيبت في سبيل الله فقال إن شئت دعوت الله فرد عليك عينك وإن شئت فعين في الجنة قال عين في الجنة قال هذا غريب لا نعرفه إلا من هذا الوجه قلت فيه لفظة منكرة فإن أبا سفيان في حصار الطائف كان مسلما فكيف يرمي سعيدا إن كان سعيد مسلما وأظن الصواب أن أبا سفيان رماه سعيد ويؤيد ذلك ما أخرجه الزبير بن بكار من هذا الوجه فقال عن سعيد بن عبيد قال رأيت أبا سفيان يوم الطائف قاعدا في حائط يأكل فرميته فأصبت عينه فذكر الحديث وروى بن عائذ عن الوليد عن سعيد بن عبد العزيز أن عين أبي سفيان أصيبت يوم الطائف وروى أبو الفرج الأصبهاني من طريق أسامة بن زيد الليثي عن القاسم بن محمد قال لم يزل السهم الذي أصاب عبد الله بن أبي بكر حتى قدم وفد الطائف فأراهم إياه فقال سعيد بن عبيد هذا سهمي أنا بريته وأنا رميت به فقال أبو بكر الحمد لله الذي أكرمه بيدك ولم يهنك بيده وله طريق أخرى في ترجمة عبد الله بن أبي بكر فثبتت بذلك صحبة سعيد بن عبيد وتحررت الرواية الأولى والحمد لله
records.english:
ibn ʿIlāj ibn Abī Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Ghayra ibn ʿAwf ibn Thaqīf, al-Thaqafī, the grandfather of Ismāʿīl ibn Ṭurayḥ the poet.

Ibn Manda narrated through Ismāʿīl: “My father related to me, from my grandfather, that Abū Sufyān shot an arrow at Saʿīd ibn ʿUbayd, his grandfather, on the day of al-Ṭāʾif and struck his eye. He came to the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم and said, ‘Messenger of God, this eye of mine has been struck in the path of God.’ He said, ‘If you wish, I shall pray to God and He will restore your eye to you; and if you wish, you shall have an eye in Paradise.’ He said, ‘An eye in Paradise.’” He said: “This is an unusual report; we know it only through this route.”

I say: It contains a problematic expression, for Abū Sufyān was a Muslim during the siege of al-Ṭāʾif. How, then, could he shoot Saʿīd if Saʿīd was a Muslim? I think the correct reading is that Abū Sufyān was shot by Saʿīd. This is supported by what al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār transmitted through this same route, saying, from Saʿīd ibn ʿUbayd: “I saw Abū Sufyān on the day of al-Ṭāʾif sitting in a walled garden, eating. I shot at him and struck his eye.” He then related the report.

Ibn ʿĀʾidh narrated from al-Walīd, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, that Abū Sufyān’s eye was struck on the day of al-Ṭāʾif. Abū al-Faraj al-Aṣbahānī narrated through Usāma ibn Zayd al-Laythī, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, who said: “The arrow that struck ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr remained until the delegation from al-Ṭāʾif arrived. He showed it to them, and Saʿīd ibn ʿUbayd said, ‘This is my arrow. I fashioned it and I shot it.’ Abū Bakr said, ‘الحمد لله, who honored him at your hand and did not humiliate you at his.’” It has another route in the biography of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr. Thus Saʿīd ibn ʿUbayd’s companionship is established, and the first narration has been clarified, والحمد لله.

names.arabic: سعيد بن عبيد بن أبي أسيد
names.english: Saʿīd ibn ʿUbayd ibn Abī Usayd

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

title.arabic: سعيد بن عبيد بن أبي أسيد
title.english: Saʿīd ibn ʿUbayd ibn Abī Usayd

records.arabic: تقدم في سعد وهو أصح وقد روى بن أبي شيبة ما يدل على أنه سعيد وأنه غير سعد الذي مر فقال حدثنا أبو إدريس عن إسماعيل عن الشعبي قال قرأ القرآن على عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أبي ومعاذ وزيد وأبو الدرداء وسعيد بن عبيد الحديث
records.english: Previously mentioned under Saʿd, which is the more correct form. Ibn Abī Shayba, however, narrated something indicating that he was Saʿīd and that he was a different person from the Saʿd previously mentioned. He said: “Abū Idrīs related to us, from Ismāʿīl, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: ‘Ubayy, Muʿādh, Zayd, Abū al-Dardāʾ, and Saʿīd ibn ʿUbayd recited the Qurʾān during the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وسلم lifetime’”—the report.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: يأتي ذكره في ترجمة سليط بن سليط
records.english: He will be mentioned in the biography of Salīṭ ibn Salīṭ.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الأنصاري شهد أحدا روى إسحاق بن راهويه في مسنده من طريق الزبير قال والله إني لأسمع قول معتب بن قشير والنعاس يغشاني لو كان لنا من الأمر شيء ما قتلنا ها هنا ثم قال وقوله إن الذين تولوا منكم يوم التقى الجمعان قال منهم عثمان بن عفان وسعيد بن عثمان وعلقمة بن عثمان الأنصاريان قال بلغوا جبلا بناحية المدينة ببطن الأعوص فأقاموا هناك ثلاثا قلت ساقه بن إسحاق في مسنده مع إدراجه ومن قوله ثم الخ من كلام بن إسحاق في المغازي
records.english:
al-Anṣārī. He was present at Uḥud. Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh narrated in his Musnad through al-Zubayr, who said: “By God, I could hear Muʿattib ibn Qushayr saying, while drowsiness was overcoming me, ‘If we had had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here.’” Then he said, concerning His words, “Those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met”: “Among them were ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, and the two Anṣārīs Saʿīd ibn ʿUthmān and ʿAlqama ibn ʿUthmān.” He said: “They reached a mountain in the vicinity of Medina, in the valley of al-Aʿwaṣ, and stayed there for three days.”

I say: Ibn Isḥāq presented it in his Musnad with the interpolated material included. From his words “Then,” and so forth, it is Ibn Isḥāq’s wording in al-Maghāzī.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الأنصاري ذكره الأموي فيمن استشهد يوم اليمامة واستدركه بن فتحون وقد تقدم نظيره في سعد بن عثمان فما أدرى أهما أخوان أم واحد اختلف في اسمه
records.english: al-Anṣārī. Al-Umawī mentioned him among those martyred on the day of al-Yamāma, and Ibn Fatḥūn added him as a supplementary entry. A similar notice has already appeared under Saʿd ibn ʿUthmān. I do not know whether they were two brothers or one man whose name was reported differently.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: آخر تقدم في سعد
records.english: another person, previously mentioned under Saʿd.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: حليف بني سهم ذكره موسى بن عقبة وابن إسحاق في مهاجرة الحبشة وقال موسى بن عقبة استشهد بأجنادين هو وأخوه لأمه تميم بن الحارث بن قيس وكذا قال الزبير قاله الذهبي وذكره بن سعد فيمن تقدم إسلامه ولم يشهد بدرا وسماه الواقدي وأبو معشر وأبو الأسود عن عروة سعيدا فالله أعلم
records.english: an ally of Banū Sahm. Mūsā ibn ʿUqba and Ibn Isḥāq mentioned him among those who emigrated to Abyssinia. Mūsā ibn ʿUqba said that he and his maternal brother, Tamīm ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Qays, were martyred at Ajnādayn. Al-Zubayr said the same, as al-Dhahabī related. Ibn Saʿd mentioned him among those who embraced Islam early but did not take part in Badr. Al-Wāqidī and Abū Maʿshar, and Abū al-Aswad reporting from ʿUrwa, named him Saʿīd. فالله أعلم.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الأنصاري أخو الحارث قال بن السكن له صحبة وقال بن فتحون ذكره بن عبد البر في ترجمة أخيه الحارث ولم يفرده بترجمة قلت بل قال أبو عمر في ترجمة أخيه زيد بن عمرو لا يثبت لسعيد صحبة
records.english: al-Anṣārī, the brother of al-Ḥārith. Ibn al-Sakan said: “He had companionship.” Ibn Fatḥūn said: “Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr mentioned him in the biography of his brother al-Ḥārith but did not give him a separate biography.” I say: Rather, Abū ʿUmar said in the biography of his brother Zayd ibn ʿAmr: “Companionship is not established for Saʿīd.”

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره بن الأثير عن بن ماكولا إلا أنه قال روى حديثه محمد بن المطلب عن علي بن قرين عن عبيدة بن حريث الكندي عن الصلت بن حبيب الشني عنه قال شهدت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
records.english: Ibn al-Athīr mentioned him on Ibn Mākūlā’s authority, except that he said: “His report was narrated by Muḥammad ibn al-Muṭṭalib, from ʿAlī ibn Qurayn, from ʿUbayda ibn Ḥurayth al-Kindī, from al-Ṣalt ibn Ḥabīb al-Shannī, from him. He said: ‘I was present with the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم.’”

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بالمهملة ثم التحتانية المحاربي ذكره أبو عبيد فيمن وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من قومه قال الرشاطي لم يذكره أبو عمر ولا بن فتحون
records.english: With an undotted ʿayn followed by yāʾ; al-Muḥāribī. Abū ʿUbayd mentioned him among those of his people who came in a delegation to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. Al-Rushāṭī said: “Neither Abū ʿUmar nor Ibn Fatḥūn mentioned him.”

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: قيل هو اسم أبي كبشة الأنماري فيما جزم به بن حبان وسيأتي بيان الاختلاف في اسمه في الكنى
records.english: It is said to be the name of Abū Kabshah al-Anmārī, as Ibn Ḥibbān stated definitively. The disagreement over his name will be explained in the section on kunyās.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الأزدي حليف بني عبد مناف يقال ولاه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على جرش أخرجه أبو عمر
records.english: Al-Azdī, an ally of Banū ʿAbd Manāf. It is said that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم appointed him over Jurash. Abū ʿUmar included him.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن صخر بن حرام بن ربيعة بن عدي بن غنم بن كعب بن سلمة الأنصاري السلمي ذكره أبو الأسود عن عروة فيمن شهد بدرا
records.english: Ibn Ṣakhr ibn Ḥarām ibn Rabīʿah ibn ʿAdī ibn Ghanm ibn Kaʿb ibn Salima, al-Anṣārī al-Salamī. Abū al-Aswad mentioned him, reporting from ʿUrwa, among those who took part in Badr.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: العجلي ذكر سيف والطبري أن المثنى بن حارثة استعمله بالعراق سنة اثنتي عشرة وكان من أشد الناس على الأنصاري بني تغلب واستدركه بن فتحون وقد تقدم أنهم لم يكونوا يؤمرون إلا الصحابة
records.english:
Al-ʿIjlī. Sayf and al-Ṭabarī mentioned that al-Muthannā ibn Ḥāritha appointed him in Iraq in the year twelve. He was among those most severe against [the Christians of Banū Taghlib].

Editorial note: The bracketed description follows the alternative edition’s نصارى بني تغلب. The Arabic source retained here instead reads الأنصاري بني تغلب, whose syntax is unclear; its wording has not been altered.

Ibn Fatḥūn added him as a supplementary entry. It has already been stated that they appointed only Companions to command.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: المزني أحد الإخوة ذكره الطبري في الصحابة وروى سيف في الفتوح أن خالد بن الوليد أمره على شيء من العراق حين توجه إلى الشام في خلافة أبي بكر
records.english: Al-Muzanī, one of the brothers. Al-Ṭabarī mentioned him among the Companions. Sayf narrated in al-Futūḥ that Khālid ibn al-Walīd placed him in command of part of Iraq when he set out for Syria during Abū Bakr’s caliphate.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن محمد بن عقبة بن أحيحة بن الجلاح الأنصاري ذكره بن حبان في الصحابة
records.english: Ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUqbah ibn Uḥayḥah ibn al-Julāḥ al-Anṣārī. Ibn Ḥibbān mentioned him among the Companions.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: مولى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر الخطيب في المتفق من طريق موسى بن سليمان الإيادي عن عمر بن قيس بن الماصر عن عطاء عن سعيد بن مينا مولى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول فر من المجذوم فرارك من الأسد
records.english: The client of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. Al-Khaṭīb mentioned in al-Muttafiq, through Mūsā ibn Sulaymān al-Iyādī, from ʿUmar ibn Qays ibn al-Māṣir, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Saʿīd ibn Mīnā, a client of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم: “I heard the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم say, ‘Flee from a person with leprosy as you flee from a lion.’”

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن الحارث بن عبد المطلب بن هاشم بن عم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حديثا في الاستئذان وعنه عمار بن أبي عمار ذكره بن منده وقال أبو نعيم هو عندي مرسل قلت كلام الدارقطني يدل على أنه سعيد بن الحارث أخو نوفل فالله أعلم
records.english:
Ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim; the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وسلم paternal cousin.

Editorial note: The kinship phrase means “paternal cousin,” but its attachment within the preceding genealogy is uncertain. The later proposal identifies Saʿīd as al-Ḥārith’s son and Nawfal’s brother. These two genealogical descriptions have not been reconciled; no extra generation has been supplied.

He narrated from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم a report concerning asking permission to enter, and ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār narrated from him. Ibn Manda mentioned him. Abū Nuʿaym said: “In my view, it is mursal.” I say: Al-Dāraquṭnī’s words indicate that he is Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥārith, Nawfal’s brother. فالله أعلم.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عنكثة بن عامر بن مخزوم القرشي المخزومي قال النسائي وغيره له صحبة وكان اسمه الصرم ويقال أصرم حكاه البخاري والعسكري وقال الزبير كان له ولدان هود والحكم وكان يكنى أبا هود وقال بن سعد كان يكنى أبا الحكم وأمه لبني بنت سعيد بن رياب السهمية فغيره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم روى حديثه أبو داود من رواية ابنه عبد الرحمن عنه وروى عنه أيضا بن له آخر اسمه عثمان وروى البغوي وابن منده من طريق عمر بن عثمان بن عبد الرحمن بن سعيد بن الصرم حدثني جدي عن أبيه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له أينا أكبر أنا أو أنت قال أنت أكبر وأخير مني وأنا أقدم سنا وغير اسمه فسماه سعيدا وقال الصرم قد ذهب قال بن منده غريب لا نعرفه إلا بهذا الإسناد قلت بعضه عند أبي داود وأخرج البغوي في ترجمة الصرم من حرف الصاد حديثا آخر من هذا الوجه وقال الزبير وغيره أسلم يوم الفتح وقيل قبله يكنى أبا هود وشهد حنينا وأعطى من غنائمها وروى البخاري في تاريخه من طريق يحيى بن سعيد الأنصاري قال أصيب سعيد بن يربوع ببصره فعاده عمر زاد غيره فقال له لا تدع شهود الجمعة والجماعة فقال ليس لي قائد فبعث إليه غلاما من السبي قال الزبير وهو أحد الأربعة الذين أمرهم عمر بتجديد أنصاب الحرم وروى الواقدي من طريق نافع بن جبير أن عمر لما قدم الشام فوجد الطاعون واستشار مشيخة قريش كان منهم مخرمة بن نوفل وسعيد بن يربوع وحكيم بن حزام وغيرهم قال وكان الذي كلمه في الرجوع مخرمة بن نوفل وأخبره أن قوما من قريش كانوا ثمانين رجلا خرجوا تجارا فطرقهم الطاعون فماتوا أجمعين في ليلة إلا رجلين أحدهما صفوان بن نوفل يعني أخاه قال الزبير وغيره مات سنة أربع وخمسين وله مائة وعشرون سنة وقيل وزيادة أربع
records.english:
Ibn ʿAnkathah ibn ʿĀmir ibn Makhzūm, al-Qurashī al-Makhzūmī. Al-Nasāʾī and others said that he had companionship. His name was al-Ṣarm; it is also said to have been Aṣram, as al-Bukhārī and al-ʿAskarī related. Al-Zubayr said that he had two sons, Hūd and al-Ḥakam, and that his kunyā was Abū Hūd. Ibn Saʿd said that his kunyā was Abū al-Ḥakam and that his mother was Lubnī bint Saʿīd ibn Riyāb al-Sahmiyya. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم changed his name.

Abū Dāwūd narrated his report through his son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from him. Another son of his, named ʿUthmān, also narrated from him. Al-Baghawī and Ibn Manda narrated through ʿUmar ibn ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿīd ibn al-Ṣarm: “My grandfather related to me, from his father, that the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said to him, ‘Which of us is older, you or I?’ He replied, ‘You are greater and better than I, while I am more advanced in years.’ He changed his name, calling him Saʿīd, and said, ‘Al-Ṣarm has gone.’” Ibn Manda said: “An unusual report; we know it only through this chain.” I say: Part of it is in Abū Dāwūd. Al-Baghawī transmitted another report through this route in the biography of al-Ṣarm under the letter ṣād.

Al-Zubayr and others said that he embraced Islam on the day of the Conquest, or, it is said, before it; his kunyā was Abū Hūd. He took part in Ḥunayn and was given a share of its spoils. Al-Bukhārī narrated in his History, through Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī, who said: “Saʿīd ibn Yarbūʿ was afflicted in his eyesight, and ʿUmar visited him.” Someone else added: “He said to him, ‘Do not give up attending Friday prayer and the congregational prayer.’ He replied, ‘I have no one to lead me.’ So he sent him a boy from among the captives.” Al-Zubayr said that he was one of the four whom ʿUmar ordered to renew the boundary markers of the Sacred Precinct.

Al-Wāqidī narrated through Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr that, when ʿUmar arrived in Syria, encountered the plague, and consulted the elders of Quraysh, they included Makhrama ibn Nawfal, Saʿīd ibn Yarbūʿ, Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām, and others. He said: “The one who spoke to him about returning was Makhrama ibn Nawfal. He told him that a party of Quraysh, numbering eighty men, had gone out as merchants. The plague struck them, and they all died in one night except for two men, one of whom was Ṣafwān ibn Nawfal,” meaning his brother. Al-Zubayr and others said that he died in the year fifty-four at the age of one hundred and twenty, or, it is said, four years more.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: نزل مصر قال بن يونس في تاريخ الغرباء هو من أهل فلسطين كان أميرا على مصر ليزيد بن معاوية روى عنه من أهل مصر أبو الخير مرثد اليزني ثم ساق من طريق الليث وكذلك الحسن بن سفيان من طريق يزيد بن أبي حبيب عن أبي الخير عن سعيد بن يزيد أن رجلا قال يا رسول الله أوصني قال أوصيك أن تستحي من الله كما تستحي رجلا صالحا من قومك ورواه بن أبي خيثمة من طريق بن لهيعة عن يزيد بن أبي الخير عن سعيد بن فلان وقال أبو عمر زعم أبو الخير أن له صحبة والذي رأينا من روايته فعن بن عمر انتهى وذكر بن أبي حاتم أنه اختلف فيه على عبد الحميد بن جعفر فروى بعضهم يعني بالسند عنه عن سعيد بن مرثد عن بن عم له قال قلت يا رسول الله وفي المراسيل لابن أبي حاتم سمعت أبي يقول كنا لا ندري له صحبة أو لا فروى عنه عبد الحميد بن جعفر عن أبي الخير عن سعيد بن يزيد رجل من الصحابة حديث استحي من ربك قال فدلنا على أن لا صحبة له فعلى قوله يكون الصواب فيما قاله أبو عمر فعن بن عمر تصحيفا وقد حكى أبو عمر الكندي أن رؤساء أهل مصر لما أمر عليهم قالوا ما كان في زماننا شاب مثله فهذا يدل على أن لا صحبة له
records.english:
He settled in Egypt. Ibn Yūnus said in his History of Outsiders: “He was from Palestine and was governor of Egypt for Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiya. Among the Egyptians, Abū al-Khayr Marthad al-Yazanī narrated from him.” He then gave a report through al-Layth, and al-Ḥasan ibn Sufyān likewise gave it through Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Abū al-Khayr, from Saʿīd ibn Yazīd: “A man said, ‘Messenger of God, counsel me.’ He said, ‘I counsel you to feel shame before God as you would before a righteous man of your people.’”

Ibn Abī Khaythama narrated it through Ibn Lahīʿa, from Yazīd ibn Abī al-Khayr, from Saʿīd ibn so-and-so. Abū ʿUmar said: “Abū al-Khayr claimed that he had companionship. What we have seen of his narration, however, is from Ibn ʿUmar.” End of quotation.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim mentioned that accounts of it differed in transmission from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Jaʿfar. Some narrated it—meaning, with the chain from him—from Saʿīd ibn Marthad, from a paternal cousin of his, who said: “I said, ‘Messenger of God …’” In Ibn Abī Ḥātim’s al-Marāsīl: “I heard my father say, ‘We did not know whether he had companionship or not. Then ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Jaʿfar narrated from him, from Abū al-Khayr, from Saʿīd ibn Yazīd, a man among the Companions, the report “Feel shame before your Lord.”’ He said: ‘This showed us that he did not have companionship.’” According to his statement, Abū ʿUmar’s words “from Ibn ʿUmar” would be a textual misreading.

Editorial note: The chains and pronouns in this passage are uncertain. The source calls Saʿīd ibn Yazīd “a man among the Companions” and then gives a negative conclusion about companionship without securely identifying its referent. The alternative edition instead has Saʿīd ibn Yazīd narrating “from a man among the Companions” and explicitly proposes “from a paternal cousin of his” for “from Ibn ʿUmar.” Those readings explain that edition’s argument but have not been inserted into the source reproduced here.

Abū ʿUmar al-Kindī related that, when he was appointed over the Egyptians, their leading men said: “There has not been a young man like him in our time.” This indicates that he did not have companionship.

records.arabic: ذكره بن أبي خيثمة وابن شاهين في الصحابة وغايرا بينه وبين الذي قبله ووحدهما غيرهما
records.english: Ibn Abī Khaythamah and Ibn Shāhīn mentioned him among the Companions and distinguished him from the preceding man, while others identified the two as one person.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: أو فلان بن سعيد روى الحسن بن سفيان من طريق يونس بن أبي يعقوب عن أبيه قال جلست أنا وجعفر بن عمرو بن حريث وسعيد بن أشوع إلى فلان بن سعيد أو سعيد بن فلان فحدثنا أن نفرا أتوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا يا رسول الله أرنا رجالا من أهل الجنة قال أنا من أهل الجنة وأبو بكر وعمر فسمى جماعة قال فقال فلان بن سعيد أو سعيد بن فلان وأنا من أهل الجنة قلت أورده الحسن بن سفيان في مسند سعيد بن زيد وفيه نظر لأن بن أشوع لم يدركه فإن كان محفوظا فهو غيره
records.english:
Or so-and-so ibn Saʿīd.

Editorial note: Sʿydā is a letter-based rendering of the anomalous written سعيدا; ā represents its terminal alif. It does not establish a separate name pronounced Saʿīdā, a particular case ending, or a repaired Saʿīd. The alternative edition writes سعيد without that alif, but it also retains the uncertain naming order. Neither spelling establishes the man’s identity or equates him with Saʿīd ibn Zayd.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Sufyān narrated through Yūnus ibn Abī Yaʿqūb, from his father, who said: “I sat, together with Jaʿfar ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth and Saʿīd ibn Ashwaʿ, with so-and-so ibn Saʿīd, or Saʿīd ibn so-and-so. He told us that a group came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and said, ‘Messenger of God, point out to us men who belong to Paradise.’ He said, ‘I belong to Paradise, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar,’ and he named a number of people.” He said: “Then so-and-so ibn Saʿīd, or Saʿīd ibn so-and-so, said, ‘And I belong to Paradise.’” I say: Al-Ḥasan ibn Sufyān included it in the musnad of Saʿīd ibn Zayd. This is questionable, because Ibn Ashwaʿ did not reach his time. If the report is accurately preserved, then this is someone else.

records.arabic: والد ميسرة يأتي ذكره في ترجمة مولاته كثيرة بنت سفيان
records.english: The father of Maysarah. He will be mentioned in the biography of his patroness, Kathīra bint Sufyān.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: والد عبد العزيز جاءت عنه عدة أحاديث من رواية ولده عنه تفرد بها عبد الغفور أبو الصباح بن عبد العزيز عن أبيه عبد العزيز عن أبيه سعيد منها ما أخرجه بن عدي من طريق عامر بن سيار عن أبي الصباح بهذا الإسناد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لا يجمع الإيمان والبخل في قلب رجل مؤمن أبدا قال بن عدي وبهذا الإسناد اثنان وعشرون حديثا وأخرج له بن منده من طريق بقية عن عبد الغفور بهذا الإسناد قال فيه عن أبيه وكان من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكر حديثا آخر وأخرج له بن قانع حديثا من رواية صالح بن مالك عن عبد الغفور عن عبد العزيز عن أبيه قال صليت خلف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فكنت قريبا منه الحديث وأخرج له آخر نسبه فيه أنصاريا وسيأتي أبو عبد العزيز في الكنى في حديث وهو هذا أخرجه الطبري في التفسير وابن أبي عاصم في الوحدان وأورد البخاري في كتاب الضعفاء في ترجمة عبد الغفور من رواية عثمان بن مطر عنه عن عبد العزيز بن سعيد عن أبيه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن الله يمسخ خلقا كثيرا وإن الإنسان يخلو بمعصية فيقول الله تعالى استهان بي فيمسخه ثم يبعثه يوم القيامة إنسانا يقول له كما بدأكم تعودون ثم يدخله النار وله عند بقي بن مخلد أربعة أحاديث
records.english:
The father of ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz. Several hadiths have been transmitted from him through his son’s narration from him. They were transmitted solely by ʿAbd al-Ghafūr Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from his father ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from his father Saʿīd.

Among them is what Ibn ʿAdī transmitted through ʿĀmir ibn Sayyār, from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ, with this chain, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, who said: “Faith and miserliness never come together in the heart of a believing man.” Ibn ʿAdī said: “There are twenty-two reports with this chain.” Ibn Manda transmitted a report of his through Baqiyya, from ʿAbd al-Ghafūr, with this chain, in which he said: “From his father, who was one of the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وسلم Companions.” He then related another report.

Ibn Qāniʿ transmitted a report of his through Ṣāliḥ ibn Mālik, from ʿAbd al-Ghafūr, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from his father, who said: “I prayed behind the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and was close to him”—the report continues. He transmitted another report of his in which he described him as an Anṣārī. Abū ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz will appear in the section on kunyās in connection with a report, and he is this man. Al-Ṭabarī transmitted it in his Qurʾān commentary, and Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim in al-Wuḥdān.

In the Book of Weak Narrators, under ʿAbd al-Ghafūr’s biography, al-Bukhārī cited, through ʿUthmān ibn Maṭar, from him, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Saʿīd, from his father, that the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said: “God turns many creatures into other forms. A person commits a sin in private, and God تعالى says, ‘He has treated Me with contempt,’ and transforms him. Then He raises him on the Day of Resurrection as a human being, saying to him, ‘As He first created you, you shall return.’ Then He causes him to enter the Fire.” Baqī ibn Makhlad has four reports from him.

names.arabic: عبد الغفور أبو الصباح بن عبد العزيز
names.english: ʿAbd al-Ghafūr Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz

records.arabic: بالتصغير تقدم في سعيد بن سهل
records.english: In the diminutive. He was previously discussed under Saʿīd ibn Sahl.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: مصغرا آخره راء بن خفاف التميمي ذكره سيف في الفتوح وأنه كان عاملا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على بطون تميم وأقره أبو بكر
records.english: In the diminutive, ending in rāʾ; ibn Khufāf al-Tamīmī. Sayf mentioned him in al-Futūḥ and stated that he was an official of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم over clans of Tamīm and that Abū Bakr retained him in office.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: العامري وقيل هو سفيان روى بن منده من طريق العلاء بن الفضل عن أبي سويد المنقري عن آبائه أن سعير بن سوادة أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
records.english: Al-ʿĀmirī; it is also said that he is Sufyān. Ibn Manda narrated through al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Faḍl, from Abū Suwayd al-Minqārī, from his forefathers, that Suʿayr ibn Sawādah came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الفريعي ويقال البكائي ذكره المدائني في كتاب رسل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وروى من طريق عبد الله بن يحيى قال أراني بن لسعير بن العداء كتابا من محمد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كتبه لسعير بن عداء ورواه الباوردي وابن منده من هذا الوجه وزاد إني أخفرتك الرجيح
records.english:
Al-Furayʿī, also called al-Bakkāʾī. Al-Madāʾinī mentioned him in the Book of the Envoys of the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم. He narrated through ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā, who said: “A son of Suʿayr ibn al-ʿAddāʾ showed me a letter from Muḥammad, the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم, which he had written for Suʿayr ibn ʿAddāʾ.” Al-Bāwardī and Ibn Manda narrated it through this route, adding: “I [أخفرتك الرجيح: the wording and meaning are uncertain].”

Editorial note: The source’s full closing clause is إني أخفرتك الرجيح. Its verb does not securely establish a grant of protection, and the last word’s identity and relation to the verb are unclear. The alternative edition instead prints احضرتك الوجيح; this difference does not settle the intended clause. No positive or negative pledge has been inferred.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بفتح أوله وسكون ثانيه وفتح المثناة التحتانية بعدها هاء التأنيث بن العريض وقيل بالنون تقدم قريبا
records.english: With a fatḥah on its first letter, a sukūn on its second, and a fatḥah on the yāʾ with two dots below, followed by the feminine hāʾ—ibn al-ʿArīḍ. It is also reported with nūn. He was mentioned shortly before.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الغافقي رجل من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم شهد فتح مصر ذكره يونس وقال ذكروه في كتبهم
records.english: Al-Ghāfiqī, a man among the Companions of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, took part in the conquest of Egypt. Yūnus mentioned him and said, “They mentioned him in their books.”

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بفتحتين أو أسيد بوزن عظيم الحضرمي ذكره بن أبي خيثمة وابن أبي عاصم وغيرهما في الصحابة وأخرجه من رواية بقية أخبرني ضباره بفتح المعجمة والموحدة المخففه بن مالك الحضرمي أنه سمع أباه يحدث عن عبد الرحمن بن جبير أن أباه حدثه عن سفيان بن أسد الحضرمي أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول كبرت خيانة أن تحدث أخاك حديثا هو لك به مصدق وأنت له كاذب قال بن منده غريب وذكر بن عدي أن محمد بن ضبارة رواه عن أبيه متابعا لبقية ورواه يزيد بن شريح عن جبير بن نفير فقال عن النواس بن سمعان فالله أعلم
records.english: With two fatḥahs; or Asīd, on the pattern of ʿaẓīm; al-Ḥaḍramī. Ibn Abī Khaythamah, Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim, and others mentioned him among the Companions. The report was transmitted through Baqiyyah: “Ḍabārah”—with fatḥah on the dotted letter ḍād and on the ungeminated bāʾ—“ibn Mālik al-Ḥaḍramī informed me that he heard his father relate, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr, that his father related to him, from Sufyān ibn Asad al-Ḥaḍramī, that he heard the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم say: ‘It is a grave betrayal to tell your brother something that he believes you about while you are lying to him.’” Ibn Mandah said, “It is an isolated report.” Ibn ʿAdī mentioned that Muḥammad ibn Ḍabārah narrated it from his father, corroborating Baqiyyah. Yazīd ibn Shurayḥ narrated it from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, but gave it as “from al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān.” فالله أعلم.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن أبي سفيان بن أمية بن عبد شمس القرشي الزهري ذكره البلاذري وقال هو الذي ذهب بموت علي إلى أهل الحجاز ولا عقب له ومات أبوه كافرا وكان بن عم أبي سفيان بن حرب وأما ولده سفيان صاحب الترجمة فمقتضى ما قالوا إنه لم يبق بمكة قرشي بعد الفتح إلا أسلم وحج مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حجة الوداع أن يكون له صحبة
records.english: Ibn Abī Sufyān ibn Umayyah ibn ʿAbd Shams al-Qurashī al-Zuhrī. Al-Balādhurī mentioned him and said, “He was the one who carried the news of ʿAlī’s death to the people of the Ḥijāz. He had no descendants.” His father died an unbeliever and was a paternal cousin of Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb. As for his son Sufyān, the subject of this biography, their statement that after the conquest no Qurashī remained in Mecca without embracing Islam and performing the Farewell Pilgrimage with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم implies that he was a Companion.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: يأتي في نسر بنون ومهملة
records.english: He will appear under Nasr, with nūn and an undotted sīn.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الأنصاري من بني النبيت ذكره بن أبي حاتم عن أبيه في الصحابة وقال بن شاهين عن الواقدي استشهد ببئر معونة
records.english: Al-Anṣārī, of Banū al-Nabīt. Ibn Abī Ḥātim, reporting from his father, mentioned him among the Companions. Ibn Shāhīn, reporting from al-Wāqidī, said that he was martyred at Biʾr Maʿūnah.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن أمية بن رافع بن سويد بن حرام بن الهيثم بن ظفر الأنصاري الظفري قال بن شاهين عن بن الكلبي إنه شهد أحدا واستشهد ببئر معونة
records.english: Ibn Umayyah ibn Rāfiʿ ibn Suwayd ibn Ḥarām ibn al-Haytham ibn Ẓafar al-Anṣārī al-Ẓafarī. Ibn Shāhīn, reporting from Ibn al-Kalbī, said that he took part in Uḥud and was martyred at Biʾr Maʿūnah.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الثقفي مر في الحكم بن سفيان
records.english: Al-Thaqafī. He was previously discussed under al-Ḥakam ibn Sufyān.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عبد عمرو بن خولى بن همام العبدي ذكر بن الكلبي أن له وفادة وقال الرشاطي في الحدادي بضم المهملة لم يذكره أبو عمر ولا بن فتحون
records.english: Ibn ʿAbd ʿAmr ibn Khawlī ibn Hammām al-ʿAbdī. Ibn al-Kalbī mentioned that he came as a member of a delegation. Al-Rushāṭī said under al-Ḥudādī—with ḍammah on the undotted letter ḥāʾ—“Neither Abū ʿUmar nor Ibn Fatḥūn mentioned him.”

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الأزدي من أزد شنوءة قال بن المديني وخليفة اسم أبيه القرد وقيل بن نمير بن مرارة بن عبد الله بن مالك ويقال فيه النمري لأنه من ولد النمر بن عثمان بن نصر بن زهران نزل المدينة وحديثه في البخاري من رواية عبد الله بن الزبير عنه وروى البخاري أيضا من طريق السائب بن يزيد عنه قال وهو رجل من أزد شنوءة من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من اقتنى كلبا الحديث
records.english:
Al-Azdī, of Azd Shanūʾah. Ibn al-Madīnī and Khalīfah said that his father’s name was al-Qird; another form given is “ibn Numayr ibn Murārah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik” [the attachment of this alternative genealogy is uncertain]. He is also called al-Namirī, because he was descended from al-Namir ibn ʿUthmān ibn Naṣr ibn Zahrān. He settled in Medina. His hadith is in al-Bukhārī, narrated by ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr from him. Al-Bukhārī also narrated through al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd from him, describing him as “a man of Azd Shanūʾah, one of the Companions of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم”: “Whoever keeps a dog ...”—the hadith.

Editorial note: The alternative genealogy in the source begins with “ibn Numayr,” without stating whose lineage is being given. The corresponding ACO passage begins the alternative with Numayr, without that initial “ibn.” The source’s wording is retained here; the relationship is not silently reconstructed.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: أو يزيد الأزدي ذكره البخاري في الصحابة وقال إن الحديث عنه منقطع وهو من رواية روح بن عوف عن بن سيرين عنه في العتيرة
records.english: Or Yazīd; al-Azdī. Al-Bukhārī mentioned him among the Companions and said that the hadith from him has a disconnected chain. It is narrated by Rawḥ ibn ʿAwf, from Ibn Sīrīn, from him, concerning the ʿatīrah sacrifice.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الحمصي ذكره عبد الصمد بن سعيد في الصحابة الذين نزلوا حمص
records.english: Al-Ḥimṣī. ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Saʿīd mentioned him among the Companions who settled in Ḥimṣ.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: أو بن أبي سهل الثقفي له ذكر في حديث المغيرة بن شعبة روى أحمد والنسائي وابن حبان وغيرهم من حديث عبد الملك بن عمير عن حصين بن عقبة عن المغيرة بن شعبة قال رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو آخذ بحجرة سفيان بن أبي سهل وهو يقول لا تسبل إزارك لفظ أحمد وعند النسائي سفيان بن سهل ومداره عندهم على شريك بن عبد الملك وقيل عن شريك بن عبد الملك وقيل عن شريك عن عبد الملك عن قبيصة بن جابر بدل حصين بن عقبة وقيل عن عبد الملك عن المغيرة بغير واسطة والأول أصح
records.english:
Or ibn Abī Sahl; al-Thaqafī. He is mentioned in a hadith of al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah. Aḥmad, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Ḥibbān, and others narrated a hadith of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿUqbah, from al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah, who said, “I saw the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم holding Sufyān ibn Abī Sahl by his [waistband], saying, ‘Do not let your waist-wrapper hang down.’” This is Aḥmad’s wording; al-Nasāʾī has “Sufyān ibn Sahl.” In their versions the chain turns on Sharīk ibn ʿAbd al-Malik. One version has “from Sharīk ibn ʿAbd al-Malik”; another has “from Sharīk, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from Qabīṣah ibn Jābir,” in place of Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿUqbah; and another has “from ʿAbd al-Malik, from al-Mughīrah,” with no intermediary. The first is more sound.

Editorial note: “Waistband” is a tentative reading supported by بحجزة in the independent ACO edition; the source writes بحجرة. In the later chain discussion, the source twice gives “Sharīk ibn ʿAbd al-Malik” before a version with “Sharīk, from ʿAbd al-Malik.” ACO also preserves that distinction. The ambiguous parentage or transmission link is left as written.

records.arabic: المهري المعروف بالخرنق الشاعر ذكره بن أبي داود في الصحابة وتبعه بن منده وغيره وذكر بن يونس أنه شهد فتح مصر وأنه قال كنت والمقداد لصين في الجاهلية
records.english: Al-Mahrī, known as al-Khirniq, the poet. Ibn Abī Dāwūd mentioned him among the Companions, followed by Ibn Mandah and others. Ibn Yūnus mentioned that he took part in the conquest of Egypt, and that he said, “Al-Miqdād and I were thieves in the pre-Islamic period.”

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن ربيعة بن الحارث بن مالك بن حطيط بن جشم الثقفي الطائفي أسلم مع الوفد وسأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أمر يعتصم به فقال قل ربي الله ثم استقم أخرج حديثه مسلم والنسائي والترمذي واستعمله عمر على صدقات الطائف ووقع في رواية مرسلة لابن أبي شيبة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم استعمله على الطائف وروى عنه أولاده عاصم وعبد الله وعلقمة وعمرو وأبو الحكم وغيرهم وقال أبو الحسن المديني شهد سفيان بن عبد الله بن ربيعة حنينا فقتل أخوه عثمان فاستقبل وقال لأبي سويد لا خير في العيش بعده فتخيل أبو سويد حتى انهزم به وذلك أنه قطع طرف عذاره وكان على حصان وأبو سويد على أنثى فأدناها من فرس سفيان حتى شمها ثم حرك أبو سويد فرسه وذهب فرس سفيان ليتبعها فلحقه سفيان ليحبسه فانقطع اللجام واستمر فرسه يتبع فرس أبي سويد فنجيا جميعا وأسلم سفيان بعد ذلك قلت ولم أقف على حال أبي سويد المذكور
records.english:
Ibn Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Mālik ibn Ḥuṭayṭ ibn Jusham al-Thaqafī al-Ṭāʾifī.

Editorial note: The source heading reads سفين. The quoted form in the English title preserves these four letters without assigning a pronunciation or treating them as a separate name. Later in the same notice the subject is called سفيان بن عبد الله, and the corresponding heading in the independent ACO edition reads سفيان. The internal ا after ي has not been restored in the title. The source’s lineage continues with “ibn Rabīʿah”; ACO instead has an additional Abī before Rabīʿah. That separate genealogy difference is not imported here.

He embraced Islam with the delegation and asked the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم for a principle to hold fast to. He replied, “Say, ‘My Lord is God,’ then remain steadfast.” Muslim, al-Nasāʾī, and al-Tirmidhī transmitted his hadith. ʿUmar appointed him to collect the alms of al-Ṭāʾif. A mursal report transmitted by Ibn Abī Shaybah states that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم appointed him over al-Ṭāʾif. His sons ʿĀṣim, ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAlqamah, ʿAmr, and Abū al-Ḥakam, and others, narrated from him.

Abū al-Ḥasan al-Madīnī said: “Sufyān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rabīʿah took part in Ḥunayn. His brother ʿUthmān was killed, so he turned to face [what he faced is not stated] and said to Abū Suwayd, ‘There is no good in life after him.’ Abū Suwayd devised a ruse until he got him to retreat with him. He did this by cutting the end of his bridle’s cheek-strap. Sufyān was on a stallion, and Abū Suwayd was on a mare, so he brought her near Sufyān’s horse until it smelled her. Then Abū Suwayd urged his horse on, and Sufyān’s horse went to follow her. Sufyān caught up with it to hold it back, but the bridle broke, and his horse kept following Abū Suwayd’s horse. They both escaped, and Sufyān embraced Islam afterward.”

I say: I have not found an account of the circumstances of the Abū Suwayd mentioned here.

Editorial note: A mursal report omits a link in its transmission to the Prophet. The phrase rendered “turned to face” is likewise without an expressed object in the corresponding ACO passage; no enemy or direction has been supplied.

records.arabic: المخزومي ذكر أبو عمر أنه من المؤلفة وفيه نظر وذكره العدوي في النسب وأنه أخو أبي سلمة ولم يذكر أنه أسلم وعند بن الكلبي ما يدل على أنه أسلم فيكتب من ترجمة ربيبته أم عمرو بنت سفيان من النساء
records.english:
Al-Makhzūmī. Abū ʿUmar stated that he was among those whose hearts were reconciled, but this is open to question. Al-ʿAdawī mentioned him in his work on genealogy and stated that he was Abū Salamah’s brother, but did not mention that he embraced Islam. Ibn al-Kalbī has material indicating that he embraced Islam; it should therefore be copied from the biography of his stepdaughter, Umm ʿAmr bint Sufyān, in the section on women.

Editorial note: “His stepdaughter” preserves the source’s relationship term, whose reference is uncertain. The women’s entry identifies Umm ʿAmr as the daughter of Sufyān ibn ʿAbd al-Asad and the sister of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sufyān. The corresponding ACO cross-reference does not settle the relationship. No different father or corrected kinship has been supplied.

records.arabic: بن أبي وقاص الزهري ينظر من القسم الثاني روى الطبراني من طريق إسماعيل بن راشد أن معاوية بعثه رسولا إلى عمرو بن العاص يخبره بقتل علي وقد تقدم في سفيان بن أمية أنه كان رسولا إلى الحجاز بمثل ذلك قال بن عساكر لم أر له ذكرا في كتب الأنساب ولا التاريخ
records.english: Ibn Abī Waqqāṣ al-Zuhrī. To be considered for the second section. Al-Ṭabarānī narrated through Ismāʿīl ibn Rāshid that Muʿāwiyah sent him as a messenger to ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ to inform him of ʿAlī’s killing. It has already been stated under Sufyān ibn Umayyah that he was a messenger to the Ḥijāz with similar news. Ibn ʿAsākir said, “I have not seen him mentioned in the books of genealogy or history.”

records.arabic: بن الحارث بن مصاد بن مازن بن ذؤيب بن كعب بن عمرو بن تميم التميمي ذكره بن سعد في الطبقات فقال أنبأنا هشام بن الكلبي قال حدثني رجل من عبد القيس قال حدثني محمد بن جناح أخو بني عمرو بن كعب بن تميم قال وفد سفيان بن العديل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأسلم فقال له ابنه قيس يا أبت دعني آت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم معك قال ومات قيس في زمن أبي بكر مع العلاء بن الحضرمي بالبحرين فقال فيه بعض الشعراء فإن يك قيس قد مضى لسبيله فقد طاب قيس بالرسول فأسلما وسيأتي ذكر ولده غنيم بن قيس في الغين المعجمة
records.english:
Ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Miṣād ibn Māzin ibn Dhuʾayb ibn Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr ibn Tamīm al-Tamīmī. Ibn Saʿd mentioned him in al-Ṭabaqāt, saying: “Hishām ibn al-Kalbī informed us, saying: A man of ʿAbd al-Qays related to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Janāḥ, a member of Banū ʿAmr ibn Kaʿb ibn Tamīm, related to me, saying: Sufyān ibn al-ʿAdīl came as a delegate to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and embraced Islam. His son Qays said to him, ‘Father, let me come to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم with you.’” He said: “Qays died in Abū Bakr’s time, with al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥaḍramī in al-Baḥrayn.” One of the poets said of him:

Though Qays has gone on his way,
Qays found joy in the Messenger, and embraced Islam.

His son Ghunaym ibn Qays will be mentioned under the dotted letter ghayn.

names.arabic: بني عمرو بن كعب بن تميم
names.english: Banū ʿAmr ibn Kaʿb ibn Tamīm

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
الجذامي كان نازلا في بني حنيفة ولم يرتد ذكر ذلك وثيمة وذكر أن خالد بن الوليد أخذه فيمن ظفر به من أهل اليمامة فأراد قتله فقال له سفيان يا خالد إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ما من عبد يقتل عبدا إلا قعد له يوم القيامة على الصراط فخلى سبيله وفيه يقول الشاعر
إنني والحصين وابن أبي عزة
سفيان ديننا الإسلام
records.english:
Al-Judhāmī. He was living among Banū Ḥanīfah and did not apostatize. Wathīmah mentioned this, and mentioned that Khālid ibn al-Walīd captured him among the people of al-Yamāmah whom he overcame and intended to kill him. Sufyān said to him, “Khālid, the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said: ‘No servant kills another servant without the latter sitting in wait for him on the Bridge on the Day of Resurrection.’” So he let him go. Of him the poet says:

As for me, al-Ḥuṣayn, and Ibn Abī ʿAzzah—
Sufyān—our religion is Islam.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن ربيعة الثقفي روى البغوي وعمه أحمد بن منيع من طريق بن إسحاق عن عيسى بن عبد الله عن سفيان بن عطية بن ربيعة الثقفي قال وفد ناس من ثقيف على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال بن أبي خيثمة هو عطية بن سفيان قدم مع وفد ثقيف قلت المحفوظ أن الحديث من رواية عيسى بن عطية بن سفيان بن ربيعة الثقفي عن بعض وفدهم فالله أعلم
records.english: Ibn Rabīʿah al-Thaqafī. Al-Baghawī transmitted—as did his uncle Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ—through Ibn Isḥāq, from ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Sufyān ibn ʿAṭiyyah ibn Rabīʿah al-Thaqafī, who said, “Some people of Thaqīf came as delegates to the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم.” Ibn Abī Khaythamah said, “He is ʿAṭiyyah ibn Sufyān; he came with the delegation of Thaqīf.” I say: The preserved version is that the hadith is narrated by ʿĪsā ibn ʿAṭiyyah ibn Sufyān ibn Rabīʿah al-Thaqafī, from some of their delegation. فالله أعلم.

names.arabic: عيسى بن عطية بن سفيان بن ربيعة
names.english: ʿĪsā ibn ʿAṭiyyah ibn Sufyān ibn Rabīʿah

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن وهب النضري تقدم في سعد بن وهب
records.english: Ibn Wahb al-Naḍrī. He was previously discussed under Saʿd ibn Wahb.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الثقفي ذكره بن أبي عاصم في الصحابة وذكره الطبراني في المعجم الكبير في الصحابة لكنه زعم أنه أبو ليلى الأنصاري والد عبد الرحمن وذكر العسكري أن جريرا روى في حديث سفيان بن أبي زهير فقال سفيان بن أبي العوجاء
records.english: Al-Thaqafī. Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim mentioned him among the Companions. Al-Ṭabarānī also mentioned him among the Companions in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr, but claimed that he was Abū Laylā al-Anṣārī, the father of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. Al-ʿAskarī mentioned that Jarīr, when narrating the hadith of Sufyān ibn Abī Zuhayr, gave the name as “Sufyān ibn Abī al-ʿAwjāʾ.”

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
الأسلمي أو الغامدي يأتي في مالك بن وهب وروى الحاكم عن مصعب الزبيري قال وسفيان بن عوف الغامدي صحب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وكان له بأس ونجدة وسخاء وهو الذي أغار على هيت والأنبار في أيام علي فقتل وسبى وإياه عنى علي بن أبي طالب في خطبته حيث قال فيها وإن أخا غامد قد أغار على هيت والأنبار وقتل حسان بن حسان يعني عامل علي واستعمل معاوية سفيان بن عوف على الصوائف وكان يعظه ثم استعمل بعده بن مسعود الفزاري فقال له الشاعر
أقم يا بن مسعود قناة صليبة
كما كان سفيان بن عوف يقيمها وروى بن عائذ من طريق صفوان بن عمرو عن الفرج بن محمد عن بعض أشياخه قال كنا مع سفيان بن عوف الغامدي سارين بأرض الروم فأغار على باب الذهب حتى حرج أهل القسطنطينية فقالوا والله ما ندري أخطأتم الحساب أم كذب الكتاب أم استعجلتم المقدر فإنا وأنتم نعلم أنها ستفتح ولكن ليس هذا زمانها وقال بن عساكر سفيان بن عوف بن المغفل بن عوف بن عمر بن كلب بن ذهل بن سيار بن والبة بن الدئل بن سعد مناة بن غامد بن الأزد الغامدي شهد فتح الشام ثم روى من طريق سفيان بن مسلم الأزدي عن سفيان بن عوف الأزدي قال بعثنا أبو عبيدة إلى عمر بكتاب وذكر خليفة أنه مات سنة ثلاث وخمسين وأبو عبيد سنة اثنتين والواقدي سنة أربع فالله أعلم وذكره بن الكلبي فقال سفيان بن عوف بن المغفل بن عوف بن عمير بن كلب بن ذهل بن سيار بن والبة بن الدول بن سعد بن زيد مناة بن غامد الغامدي صاحب الصوائف
records.english:
Al-Aslamī or al-Ghāmidī. He will appear under Mālik ibn Wahb. Al-Ḥākim narrated from Muṣʿab al-Zubayrī, who said: “Sufyān ibn ʿAwf al-Ghāmidī accompanied the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. He possessed fighting strength, courage, and generosity. He was the one who raided Hīt and al-Anbār in ʿAlī’s time, killing people and taking captives. It was he whom ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib meant in his sermon when he said, ‘The man of Ghāmid has raided Hīt and al-Anbār and killed Ḥassān ibn Ḥassān’”—meaning ʿAlī’s governor. Muʿāwiyah put Sufyān ibn ʿAwf in charge of the summer campaigns. He used to admonish him. After him he appointed Ibn Masʿūd al-Fazārī, and the poet said to him:

Hold a sturdy spear upright, Ibn Masʿūd,
as Sufyān ibn ʿAwf used to hold it upright.

Ibn ʿĀʾidh narrated through Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr, from al-Faraj ibn Muḥammad, from one of his elders, who said: “We were with Sufyān ibn ʿAwf al-Ghāmidī on a night march in Byzantine territory. He raided the Golden Gate until the people of Constantinople were in distress. They said, ‘By God, we do not know whether you have miscalculated, the book has spoken falsely, or you have hastened what was decreed. We and you know that it will be conquered, but this is not its time.’”

Ibn ʿAsākir said: “Sufyān ibn ʿAwf ibn al-Mughaffal ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿUmar ibn Kalb ibn Dhuhl ibn Sayyār ibn Wālibah ibn al-Duʾil ibn Saʿd Manāh ibn Ghāmid ibn al-Azd al-Ghāmidī took part in the conquest of Syria.” He then narrated through Sufyān ibn Muslim al-Azdī, from Sufyān ibn ʿAwf al-Azdī, who said, “Abū ʿUbaydah sent us to ʿUmar with a letter.” Khalīfah mentioned that he died in the year 53; Abū ʿUbayd gave the year “two” [52], and al-Wāqidī the year “four” [54]. فالله أعلم. Ibn al-Kalbī mentioned him as “Sufyān ibn ʿAwf ibn al-Mughaffal ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿUmayr ibn Kalb ibn Dhuhl ibn Sayyār ibn Wālibah ibn al-Dūl ibn Saʿd ibn Zayd Manāh ibn Ghāmid al-Ghāmidī, the commander of the summer campaigns.”

records.arabic: وهو بن أبي زهير تقدم
records.english: He is ibn Abī Zuhayr, previously discussed.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن المطلب القرشي المطلبي بن أخي الطفيل وعبيدة ابني الحارث لهم صحبة أخرج البغوي من طريق إبراهيم بن سعد عن سليمان بن محمد الأنصاري عن رجل من قومه يقال له الضحاك كان عالما قال آخى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بين الحارث بن عبد المطلب وسفيان بن قيس بن الحارث
records.english: Ibn al-Muṭṭalib al-Qurashī al-Muṭṭalibī, the son of the brother of al-Ṭufayl and ʿUbaydah, the two sons of al-Ḥārith. They were Companions. Al-Baghawī transmitted through Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd, from Sulaymān ibn Muḥammad al-Anṣārī, from a man of his people called al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who was learned, that he said: “The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم established a bond of brotherhood between al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and Sufyān ibn Qays ibn al-Ḥārith.”

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الثقفي ذكره الطبراني وغيره في الصحابة وأخرج من طريق عبد ربه بن الحكم عن أميمة بنت رقيقة عن رقيقة قالت جاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الطائف يطلب النصر من ثقيف فدخل على فسقية سويقا فشرب وقال لا تعبدي طاغيتهم ولا تصلي إليها فقلت إذن يقتلوني قال فإن جاءوك فقولي ربي رب هذه الطاغية ووليها ظهرك إذا صليت قالت أميمة فحدثني أخواي وهب وسفيان ابنا قيس قالا لما أسلمت ثقيف قال لنا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما فعلت أمكما قالا ماتت على الحال التي فارقتها عليها قال أسلمت أمكما إذن
records.english:
Al-Thaqafī. Al-Ṭabarānī and others mentioned him among the Companions. He transmitted through ʿAbd Rabbih ibn al-Ḥakam, from Umaymah bint Ruqayqah, from Ruqayqah, who said: “The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم came to al-Ṭāʾif seeking support from Thaqīf. He came in to [me], and [I gave him] sawīq to drink. He drank and said, ‘Do not worship their idol or pray toward it.’ I said, ‘In that case they will kill me.’ He said, ‘If they come to you, say, “My Lord is the Lord of this idol,” and turn your back to it when you pray.’” Umaymah said: “My two brothers, Wahb and Sufyān, the sons of Qays, related to me, saying: ‘When Thaqīf embraced Islam, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said to us, “What became of your mother?” We said, “She died in the state in which you left her.” He said, “Then your mother embraced Islam.”’”

Editorial note: The bracketed first-person wording follows the corresponding ACO sentence, which reads فدخل على فسقيته سويقا فشرب. The source has فدخل على فسقية سويقا فشرب. The interpretation identifies Ruqayqah as the woman visited and the giver of the drink, while preserving and disclosing the different source wording.

records.arabic: قال البغوي ذكره البخاري في الصحابة
records.english: Al-Baghawī said: Al-Bukhārī mentioned him among the Companions.

records.arabic: يقال نفير بن مجيب الثمالي قال بن عساكر سفيان أصح روى بن قانع وغيره من طريق يحيى بن أبي كثير عن أبي سلام عن حجاج بن عبيد الثمالي وكان قد رأى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وشهد معه حجة الوداع أن سفيان بن مجيب حدثه وكان من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن في جهنم سبعة آلاف واد الحديث ووقع في راوية بن قانع بخيت بموحدة ومعجمة وآخره مثناة مصغر قال الخطيب ومجيب هو الصواب ومدار حديثه على إسماعيل بن عياش عن سعيد بن يوسف عن يحيى واختلف على إسماعيل فقال أبو اليمان وغيره نفير بن مجيب وقال الهيثم بن خارجة سفيان ورجح أبو حاتم وغيره سفيان على نفير وانفرد الدارقطني فرجح نفيرا وروى بن عائذ في المغازي من طريق يزيد بن أبي حبيب قال قال عمرو بن العاص لمعاوية ابعث إلى سفيان الأزدي صاحب بعلبك ليبعث بمن خرج منهم يعني أهل مصر قال فبعث إلى السفيان بن مجيب فخرج في أثر عبد الرحمن بن عديس فأدركوهم قال وزوجه معاوية حفصة بنت أمية بن حرب وروى بن عائذ أيضا عن الوليد عن أبي مطيع أن معاوية وجه سفيان بن مجيب الثمالي إلى طرابلس في جماعة فذكر قصة
records.english:
Also called Nufayr ibn Mujīb al-Thumālī. Ibn ʿAsākir said that Sufyān is the more correct form. Ibn Qāniʿ and others narrated through Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Sallām, from Ḥajjāj ibn ʿUbayd al-Thumālī, who had seen the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and attended the Farewell Pilgrimage with him, that Sufyān ibn Mujīb, one of the Companions of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, related to him, saying: “In Gehenna there are seven thousand valleys ...”—the hadith. Ibn Qāniʿ’s version has “Bukhayt,” a diminutive, with bāʾ, the dotted khāʾ, and the two-dotted tāʾ at the end. Al-Khaṭīb said, “Mujīb is the correct form.” The chain of his hadith turns on Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh, from Saʿīd ibn Yūsuf, from Yaḥyā. The versions transmitted from Ismāʿīl differ: Abū al-Yamān and others gave “Nufayr ibn Mujīb,” while al-Haytham ibn Khārijah gave “Sufyān.” Abū Ḥātim and others preferred Sufyān to Nufayr; al-Dāraquṭnī alone preferred Nufayr.

Ibn ʿĀʾidh narrated in al-Maghāzī through Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, who said: “ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said to Muʿāwiyah, ‘Send to Sufyān al-Azdī, the man in charge of Baalbek, so that he may send for those of them who have gone out [the precise force of the command is uncertain]’”—meaning the people of Egypt. He said: “He sent to al-Sufyān ibn Mujīb, who set out in pursuit of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUdays, and they overtook them.” He said: “Muʿāwiyah married him to Ḥafṣah bint Umayyah ibn Ḥarb.” Ibn ʿĀʾidh also narrated from al-Walīd, from Abū Muṭīʿ, that Muʿāwiyah dispatched Sufyān ibn Mujīb al-Thumālī to Tripoli with a group; he then related a story.

Editorial note: The wording ليبعث بمن خرج منهم is also present in the corresponding ACO passage. The subsequent account describes pursuit and capture, but does not fully specify the action intended by the command. “Send for” is a tentative contextual rendering, not a supplied destination or an additional order.

records.arabic: بن حبيب بن وهب بن حذافة بن جمح القرشي الجمحي ذكره بن إسحاق وموسى بن عقبة عن بن شهاب في مهاجرة الحبشة وكانت معه امرأته حسنة وهي والدة شرحبيل وقال الزبير بن بكار هو أخ جميل بن معمر وذكر بن إسحاق أن معمر تبنى سفيان وكان أصله من الأنصار من بتي زريق فحالف معمر فتبناه فنسب إليه قالوا وهلك سفيان هذا وولداه جابر وجنادة في خلافة عمر
records.english:
Ibn Ḥabīb ibn Wahb ibn Ḥudhāfah ibn Jumaḥ al-Qurashī al-Jumaḥī. Ibn Isḥāq and Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, reporting from Ibn Shihāb, mentioned him among those who emigrated to Abyssinia. His wife Ḥasanah, the mother of Shuraḥbīl, was with him. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār said that he was the brother of Jamīl ibn Maʿmar. Ibn Isḥāq mentioned that Maʿmar adopted Sufyān, who was originally of the Anṣār, of [Banū] Zurayq. He entered into an alliance with Maʿmar, who adopted him, and so he was ascribed to him. They said that this Sufyān and his two sons, Jābir and Junādah, died during ʿUmar’s caliphate.

Editorial note: The source writes من بتي زريق. ACO reads من بنى زريق, supporting “of Banū Zurayq.” The bracketed group term follows that independent reading; بتي has not been changed in the Arabic or treated as an established name pronounced Batī.

records.arabic: بن زيد بن الحارث الأنصاري الخزرجي من بني جشم بن الحارث ذكره بن إسحاق فيمن شهد أحدا واختلف في أسم أبيه قال بن الكلبي والواقدي والقداح نسر بالنون والمهملة الساكنة واستصوبه بن ماكولا وقال بن إسحاق بشر بكسر الموحدة وسكون المعجمة وقال بن حبيب هو خطأ وقال أبو حاتم شهد أحد كذا قال
records.english: Ibn Zayd ibn al-Ḥārith al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī, of Banū Jusham ibn al-Ḥārith. Ibn Isḥāq mentioned him among those who took part in Uḥud. There is disagreement over his father’s name. Ibn al-Kalbī, al-Wāqidī, and al-Qaddāḥ gave “Nasr,” with nūn and an undotted sīn with sukūn; Ibn Mākūlā judged this correct. Ibn Isḥāq gave “Bishr,” with kasrah on bāʾ and sukūn on the dotted shīn. Ibn Ḥabīb said, “That is an error.” Abū Ḥātim said, “He took part in Uḥud.” That is what he said.

records.arabic: المحاربي من محارب عبد القيس وقيل من محارب خصفة والأول أصح وروى بن أبي عاصم وابن السكن والطبراني وابن شاهين من رواية يزيد بن الفضل بن عمرو بن سفيان بن همام عن أبيه عن جده عن سفيان بن همام قال قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إنه قومك عن نبيذ الجر ووقع في رواية بن السكن عن أبيه عن جده فقط واعتمد البزار هذه الرواية فأخرج الحديث في مسند عمرو بن سفيان وقال لا نعلم روى عمرو بن سفيان إلا هذا وتبعه أبو عمر فقال عمرو بن سفيان المحاربي يروي في نبيذ الجر أنه حرام يعد في الشاميين كذا قال وأما بن منده فقال عمرو بن سفيان المحاربي سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يعد في أعراب البصرة ثم ساق حديثه كما صنع البزار ثم إنه أخرج الحديث بعينه من الوجه المذكور في سفيان بن همام ولم يبينه في واحد من الموضعين على الاختلاف فيه وكذا جرى لأبي عمر فقال فيمن اسمه سفيان بن همام العبدي من عبد القيس روى في نبيذ الجر روى عنه ابنه عمرو بن سفيان ولم يبينه أيضا ولا بن الأثير
records.english:
Al-Muḥāribī, of Muḥārib of ʿAbd al-Qays; it is also said that he was of Muḥārib of Khaṣafah. The first is more correct. Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim, Ibn al-Sakan, al-Ṭabarānī, and Ibn Shāhīn narrated through Yazīd ibn al-Faḍl ibn ʿAmr ibn Sufyān ibn Hammām, from his father, from his grandfather, from Sufyān ibn Hammām, who said: “The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said to me, ‘Forbid your people to drink nabīdh prepared in jars.’” Ibn al-Sakan’s version has only “from his father, from his grandfather.” Al-Bazzār relied on this version and transmitted the hadith under the reports of ʿAmr ibn Sufyān, saying, “We know of no report narrated by ʿAmr ibn Sufyān except this one.” Abū ʿUmar followed him, saying, “ʿAmr ibn Sufyān al-Muḥāribī narrates concerning nabīdh prepared in jars that it is forbidden. He is counted among the Syrians.” That is what he said.

Ibn Mandah, however, said, “ʿAmr ibn Sufyān al-Muḥāribī heard the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. He is counted among the Bedouins of Basra.” He then gave his hadith as al-Bazzār had done. Afterward he transmitted the very same hadith by the route mentioned above under Sufyān ibn Hammām, without explaining the disagreement in either place. The same happened with Abū ʿUmar: among those named Sufyān, he listed Ibn Hammām al-ʿAbdī of ʿAbd al-Qays, saying, “He narrated concerning nabīdh prepared in jars. His son ʿAmr ibn Sufyān narrated from him.” He too did not explain it, nor did Ibn al-Athīr.

Editorial note: The source writes إنه قومك at the start of the command. The corresponding ACO passage reads انه قومك عن نبيذ الجر, supporting the imperative “Forbid your people.” The English follows that reading explicitly; the source’s Arabic letters are unchanged.

names.arabic: يزيد بن الفضل بن عمرو بن سفيان بن همام
names.english: Yazīd ibn al-Faḍl ibn ʿAmr ibn Sufyān ibn Hammām

records.arabic: الخولاني أبو أيمن قال أبو حاتم له صحبة وروى البخاري في تاريخه من طريق غياث الحراني قال مر بنا سفيان بن وهب وكانت له صحبة فسلم علينا وقال بن يونس وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وشهد فتح مصر وولي إمرة إفريقية في زمن عبد العزيز بن مروان ومات سنة اثنتين وثمانين وروى عن عمر والزبير وغيرهما روى عنه بكر بن سوادة وعبد الله بن المغيرة وأبو الخير وأبو عشانة وغيرهم وروى الحسن بن سفيان وابن شاهين من طريق سعيد بن أبي شمر السبائي سمعت سفيان بن وهب الخولاني يقول سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول لا تأت المائة وعلى ظهرها أحد باق قال فحدثت به عبد العزيز فقال لعله أراد أنه لا يبقى أحد ممن كان معه إلى رأس المائة وله في مسند أحمد حديث آخر وعند بن منده ثالث وحديثه عن عمر في مسند أبي يعلى وقال بن حبان من زعم أن له صحبة فقد وهم كذا قال في التابعين وقال قبل ذلك في الصحابة سكن مصر له صحبة وقال العجلي تابعي ثقة
records.english:
Al-Khawlānī, Abū Ayman. Abū Ḥātim said that he had Companionship. Al-Bukhārī related in his History, through Ghiyāth al-Ḥarrānī, who said: “Sufyān ibn Wahb passed by us—he had Companionship—and greeted us.” Ibn Yūnus said: “He came as a delegate to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, witnessed the conquest of Egypt, and held the governorship of Ifrīqiyah in the time of ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Marwān. He died in the year eighty-two.”

He related from ʿUmar, al-Zubayr, and others. Bakr ibn Sawādah, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, Abū al-Khayr, Abū ʿUshānah, and others related from him. Al-Ḥasan ibn Sufyān and Ibn Shāhīn related through Saʿīd ibn Abī Shamir al-Sabaʾī: “I heard Sufyān ibn Wahb al-Khawlānī say: ‘I heard the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم say: “A hundred years will not come while anyone remains on its surface.”’” He said: “I related it to ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, and he said: ‘Perhaps he meant that none of those who had been with him would remain at the completion of a hundred years.’” He has another report in Aḥmad's Musnad, and a third in Ibn Mandah's work. His report from ʿUmar is in Abū Yaʿlā's Musnad.

Ibn Ḥibbān said: “Whoever claims that he had Companionship has erred.” That is what he said in his section on the Successors, although earlier, in his section on the Companions, he had said: “He settled in Egypt; he had Companionship.” Al-ʿIjlī said: “A trustworthy Successor.”

records.english: He was previously discussed under ibn Zayd.

records.english: The father of al-Naḍr. Abū ʿUmar mentioned him briefly. He will appear in the third section.

records.arabic: مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قيل كان اسمه مهران وقيل طهمان وقيل مروان وقيل نجران وقيل رومان وقيل ذكوان وقيل كيسان وقيل سليمان وقيل سنة بالمهملة والنون وقيل بالمعجمة وقيل أيمن وقيل مرقنة وقيل أحمر وقيل أحمد وقيل رباح وقيل مفلح وقيل عمير وقيل معتب وقيل قيس وقيل عبس وقيل عيسى فهذه واحد وعشرون قولا وكان أصله من فارس فاشترته أم سلمة ثم أعتقته واشترطت عليه أن يخدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعن أم سلمة وعلي وعنه ولداه عبد الرحمن وعمر وسالم بن عبد الله بن عمر وأبو ريحانة وغيرهم قال حماد بن سلمة عن سعيد بن جهمان عن سفينة كنت مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في سفر فكان بعض القوم إذا أعى ألقى على ثوبه حتى حملت من ذلك شيئا كثيرا فقال ما أنت إلا سفينة وكان يسكن بطن نخلة
records.english:
The client of the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم. His name is said to have been Mihrān; or Ṭahmān; or Marwān; or Najrān; or Rūmān; or Dhakwān; or Kaysān; or Sulaymān; or the written form سنة, specified with an undotted sīn and a nūn; or the corresponding form with the dotted letter; or Ayman; or Marqanah; or Aḥmar; or Aḥmad; or Rabāḥ; or Mufliḥ; or ʿUmayr; or Muʿattib; or Qays; or ʿAbs; or ʿĪsā. These are twenty-one opinions.

He was originally from Persia. Umm Salamah bought him, then emancipated him on condition that he serve the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. He related from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, and from Umm Salamah and ʿAlī. His two sons, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and ʿUmar, Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, Abū Rayḥānah, and others related from him.

Ḥammād ibn Salamah related from Saʿīd ibn Jumhān, from Safīnah: “I was with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم on a journey. When one of the people grew weary, he would throw his garment onto me, until I was carrying a great deal of that. He said: ‘You are nothing but a ship!’” He used to live in Baṭn Nakhlah.

names.arabic: سالم بن عبد الله بن عمر
names.english: Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar
